title: Vollering wins stage five as Reusser retains yellow
description: Demi Vollering wins stage five of the Tour de France Femmes following a sprint victory over yellow jersey holder Marlen Reusser.
fullText:
Demi Vollering won stage five of the Tour de France Femmes following a sprint victory over yellow jersey holder Marlen Reusser.

FDJ United-Suez rider Vollering came across the line just ahead of Movistar's Reusser, after the pair overcame an initial launch to the line by Poland's Kasia Niewiadoma of Canyon-Sram.

The three riders fought out the latter stages of a demanding 140km race from Macon to Belleville-en-Beaujolais, close to Lyon, in which they pulled away from rivals with about 10km to go on the category two Mont Brouilly climb, which included a 14% gradient in places.

Switzerland's Reusser retains the overall leader's yellow jersey after winning Tuesday's time trial to Dijon, 12 seconds ahead of the Netherlands' Vollering, with Niewiadoma in third, one minute five seconds further behind.

"Today it was really cool race," said Vollering. "The whole team, every single rider was part of it. I enjoy those victories the most, when everybody put their hard work into it, it makes it more special and beautiful.

"I gave it everything to the line. It was a very long sprint and I needed every single metre in the finish straight, but I managed to do it - I am very happy about that."

It's looking increasingly likely this fifth Tour de France Femmes - since its relaunch as a stage race in 2022 - will be decided between these three riders.

Vollering is in the best form, with 11 wins this season, Reusser the most improved and Niewiadoma potentially in the best position to win Friday's much-anticipated climb up to Mont Ventoux.

It was a bitter day for defending champion and home hero Pauline Ferrand-Prevot of Visma-Lease a Bike, who lost more than two and a half minutes midway through the stage after already losing over two minutes to her main general classifiaction rivals in the time trial.

She now sits five minutes down, 17th overall.

Once dominant, Anna van der Breggan of SD Worx-Protime also lost more than two and a half minutes on the stage, as she also dropped out of contention for yellow overall - more than four minutes down.

The Netherlands' Lorena Wiebes remains in the green points jersey with 131 points, while compatriot Puck Pieterse retains the best climber's polka dot jersey despite losing ground on the stage.

Germany's Antonia Neidermaier of Canyon-Sram takes over the white young riders jersey from Spain's Paula Blasi of Team UAE L'Imad.

title: No WSL experience but who is new Man Utd boss Olid?
description: Manchester United appoint former Hearts boss Eva Olid as their new women's manager on a two-year deal, with an option for a further 12 months.
fullText:
Manchester United have confirmed Eva Olid as their new women's manager on a two-year deal with an option for a further 12 months.

The former Hearts boss replaces Marc Skinner, who left the role by mutual consent on Monday - a month before the start of the Women's Super League (WSL) season.

Having led Hearts to their first Scottish Women's Premier League (SWPL) club last campaign, Spaniard Olid, 40, opted to leave Edinburgh in the summer when her contract expired.

As well as clinching their first silverware, Olid also took Hearts to their first domestic final, but lost to Rangers in the 2024 Scottish Cup.

"The opportunity to become head coach of Manchester United Women is a dream come true," Olid said.

"There is already so much talent within our squad and I am excited to work with the players to support them to fulfil their immense potential."

Sources at Manchester United had said one of the key requirements for Skinner's replacement was a coach with a history of developing players.

It is four weeks on Friday until United begin their WSL season at London City Lionesses on 4 September.

Having arrived in Edinburgh as a virtual unknown, Olid transformed Hearts during her five years in charge.

Hearts have never been one of the main players in Scotland. When Olid left in May, they were top of the pile.

She did that thanks to a full-frontal attacking approach, based usually around a 3-4-3 formation, with her goalkeeper expected to play a key part as a fourth defender.

Hearts were top scorers in the SWPL last season with 85 goals - only Rangers with 80 were within 20 of them - so United's frontline of Ella Toone, Lea Schuller and Elisabeth Terland can hope for plenty of chances next season.

She also developed a plan B. Having failed to beat Glasgow City across her first four seasons, Olid purposefully went defensive in April's meeting and secured a 1-0 win to go top of the table.

That was the game where she announced her intention to leave, saying she could not have gone without tasting victory against them at least once.

Former Hearts captain Georgia Hunter swapped Edinburgh for Ipswich this summer and was glowing about her old boss.

"She's a great manager, very, very good," she told BBC Sport. "I learnt so much. The transition with all the players and [where] she took the club to is absolutely amazing."

Olid has a track record of developing young players too, including the Husband twins Erin and Jess, who both made their debuts under her aged 15, and United have suggested this will be important in her new role.

"Eva is the perfect coach to lead us into an exciting new era - she shares our commitment to developing exciting homegrown and young players," said United's director of women's football Matt Johnson.

Given Olid has also spent time working with the Scotland women's national team, BBC Sport Scotland's Amy Canavan was not surprised to see her secure a high profile job.

"We were convinced she had somewhere special to go," Canavan said. "She 100% deserves this chance and is ready for it."

Have Man Utd lost faith in their women's team?

Man Utd boss Skinner leaves role before WSL season

One of the most intriguing things about this appointment is that we know very little about Olid given she is untested in the WSL and in Europe.

The Spaniard was popular at Hearts and enjoyed success in the Scottish Premier League, though it is a step up to the weekly pressures of the WSL.

United's direction has been clearly laid out - they want a coach who specialises in youth development and who can improve individual players on a weekly basis.

They believe Olid meets that criteria and will hope she brings a new style of football, no doubt influenced by her Spanish roots.

Her appointment was swift following Skinner's exit, with the club already well advanced in their recruitment process and Olid's contract signed within 24 hours.

Skinner's departure also raised further questions about United's ambition for its women's team, so scrutiny on Olid will be immediate.

She will have to deal with that pressure and expectation - part of which comes naturally as United manager - but also to appease a frustrated fanbase who have demanded 

Her first job will be to galvanise a depleted squad this summer, embed youthful talent and prepare for the season opener at London City Lionesses, which will be a good marker of where United are at.

Hearts women were unusual champions. On their way to winning the SWPL title, they ranked second for build-up attacks but first for direct attacks, showing they could build both patiently and quickly.

They also saw plenty of the ball. Hearts averaged 56.8% possession, the fourth-highest figure in the league, suggesting they were often able to dictate matches rather than simply react to them.

Yet possession did not make them slow as only one team produced more shots from fast breaks. When opportunities arose, Hearts were quick to turn defence into attack.

That balance was reflected in the chances they created.

The Jambos produced 71 big chances during the season, the third-highest total in the division, while their xG per shot of 0.116 also ranked third.

In other words, they regularly fashioned good-quality opportunities rather than relying on efforts from poor positions.

Without the ball, Hearts were organised rather than overly aggressive. They ranked fifth for high turnovers and conceded only 35 big chances across the campaign, the fourth-fewest in the league.

Taken together, the numbers suggest a side capable of controlling games with the ball while remaining dangerous when opportunities to break appeared, a combination that helped power Hearts to the title.

title: Rejecting Arsenal & emulating Hazard - Monga makes debut in Man City win
description: Jeremy Monga's £10m move from Leicester to Manchester City may have gone under the radar this summer, but the teenager's own career is not expected to go in quite the same manner as he aims to emulate his idol Eden Hazard.
fullText:
Jeremy Monga's £10m move from Leicester to Manchester City may have gone under the radar this summer, but the teenager's own career is not expected to go in quite the same manner.

The 17-year-old is the third-youngest player to appear in the Premier League and now settling in at one of the world's biggest clubs, who have former Foxes boss Enzo Maresca in charge.

Monga came off the bench in City's 3-1 friendly win over a K-League XI in sweltering conditions at Seoul World Cup Stadium, with Rayan Ait-Nouri, Tijjani Reijnders and Divin Mubama on the scoresheet inside 23 minutes.

During his half an hour on the pitch, Monga showed his youthful sprightliness and almost made a dream first appearance when a close-range effort was disallowed for handball, while another curling effort was batted away by the goalkeeper.

It looked like Monga would be heading to champions Arsenal this summer as Mikel Arteta's side closed in on a deal, but the Gunners were gazumped by their title rivals.

"It [Arsenal interest] was very strong because it was very close to me going there, very close," Monga told BBC Sport.

"The main decision was probably the pathway and the club itself. They've been so successful that it was a no-brainer when City call. It's every child's dream to win trophies and be at the top with the best.

"Once I get the opportunity I just need to show myself, and once I do that, everything will take care of itself. I feel like, to me personally, I see myself at City more. I see myself in blue."

Who impressed in Man City's win over K-League XI?

Monga made his top-flight debut aged 15 years and 271 days old in Leicester's defeat by Newcastle United on 7 April, with the Foxes relegated to the Championship at the end of that season.

The 2015-16 Premier League winners then suffered a further fall from grace last term with a calamitous campaign that saw them drop into League One.

Monga played 30 times last season and took "positives" from his time at King Power Stadium as the club "gave me the foundation and stepping stone" at the start of his career.

He described the Championship as a "tough league" as defenders gave him "less time and [less] respect" compared to those in the Premier League.

"It's a dog-eat-dog world in the Championship," added England Under-19 international Monga. "They were more on me, wanting to be more physical with me and they didn't care about my age too much.

"I don't see the negatives, I see all the opportunities they [Leicester] have given me that I am thankful for. I don't like to think of the negatives, I'm just thankful."

A boyhood Chelsea supporter, Monga rates their former Belgium international Eden Hazard as his idol and is intent on emulating the forward.

When he was born in July 2009, Hazard was still a youngster at French club Lille before going on to achieve a successful career at Chelsea and Real Madrid.

Hazard won both the Premier League and La Liga twice, the Champions League in 2022, as well as being named PFA players' player of the year and Football Writers' Association (FWA) footballer of the year in 2014–15.

Asked what he admired most about Hazard, Coventry-born Monga said: "Definitely his directness, him taking the game by the scruff of his neck trying to win the game by himself and definitely the way he manipulates the ball, trying to implement that into my game.

"Even the way he protects the ball from his opponents and moves around the pitch, everything is what I want to do."

On Hazard moments that stood out? he replied: "His [solo] goal against Tottenham - or the goal against Liverpool. When you see the goal, you remember it."

If Monga goes on to achieve even half of what Hazard produced in his career, he will have done all right for himself.

title: LIV Golf secures unnamed lead investor for 2027
description: After the withdrawal of Saudi Arabian financial backing earlier this year, LIV Golf says it has secured a deal with an unnamed lead investor to continue next season.
fullText:
LIV Golf says it has secured an unnamed lead investor to keep the competition running in 2027 after the withdrawal of Saudi Arabian financial backing.

The Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF) said in April it would end its multibillion dollar backing of the brekaway tour at the end of the season, plunging the future of the series into doubt.

Chief exeuctive Scott O'Neil said a signed agreement with a new investor is in place and has been approved by the LIV Golf board, with the transaction expected to be completed in September.

No details of the amount of money that will be invested were announced. PIF has invested more than $5bn (£3.71bn) since the league launched in 2022.

O'Neil added LIV will make its players "majority equity holders" in the competition, calling it "a first for a major global sports league".

The LIV press release said the proposed deal with the lead investor is for "2027 and beyond".

Saudi Arabia to stop funding LIV Golf next season

Tours form new alliance in latest blow to LIV Golf

The competition will reduce to 10 events from next season, with five in the United States and five held around the world.

There were 14 events planned for the 2026 season but in April, LIV postponed June's New Orleans competition amid questions over its future and has not announced a rescheduled date.

O'Neil said LIV is focused on "delivering a great week for fans and players at Bedminster" in New York, starting on Sunday and "finishing the 2026 season strong" - but made no explicit mention of the final two events scheduled this season, in Indianapolis from 23 August and the concluding team championship in Michigan from 30 August.

Major winners including Bryson DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson, Jon Rahm, Cameron Smith, Martin Kaymer and Sergio Garcia remain part of the LIV roster after having left the PGA Tour.

American major champions Brooks Koepka and Patrick Reed rejoined the PGA Tour after it introduced a returning member programme.

In July, the PGA Tour and DP World Tour struck an alliance with the Asian Tour in another blow to LIV Golf.

O'Neil added: "We're also seeing strong interest from more than a dozen additional parties to potentially serve as minority investors, creating a multi-partner model built for long-term stability and growth."

LIV was founded in 2021 and launched the following year with 54-hole events and took its name from the Roman numeral for 54.

However, it moved to the traditional 72-hole format for golf tournaments from this season.

title: Celtic boss O'Neill in hospital after 'small procedure'
description: Celtic manager Martin O'Neill remains in hospital after undergoing a "small procedure", the club announce.
fullText:
Celtic manager Martin O'Neill remains in hospital after undergoing a "small procedure", the club have announced.

There are no details about the nature of O'Neill's operation, with the 74-year-old expected to be released in the "next day or two".

O'Neill signed a one-year deal in June to become permanent manager after two interim spells last season culminated in a Scottish Premiership and Scottish Cup double.

The Northern Irishman was in the dugout on Monday as Celtic started the new Premiership campaign with a 1-0 home win over Dundee.

"In response to speculation, we can confirm that Martin O'Neill has undergone a small procedure in hospital," Celtic posted on social media.

"We would envisage Martin being released from hospital in the next day or two and on behalf of Martin, we would like to thank supporters for their kind wishes.

"We would ask that the privacy of Martin and his family is respected."

Having not managed since a spell with Nottingham Forest in 2019, O'Neill made a shock return to Celtic last October - 20 years after his hugely successful first spell in charge - following Brendan Rodgers' acrimonious resignation.

The former Leicester City, Aston Villa and Republic of Ireland boss then handed the reins to Wilfried Nancy in December, but the Frenchman was sacked after just eight games, paving the way for O'Neill to return again.

And after winning his eighth and ninth major honours with the club, he agreed to take on the job full-time, agreeing a one-year contract with the option for a further year after talks with Celtic's major shareholder Dermot Desmond.

title: Real Madrid make Vinicius Jr improved contract offer
description: Real Madrid make Vinicius Jr an improved contract offer as they look to keep the Brazil winger at the Bernabeu.
fullText:
Real Madrid have made Vinicius Jr an improved contract offer as they look to keep the Brazil winger at the Bernabeu.

The 26-year-old has entered the final 12 months of his contract and has attracted interested from Arsenal in recent weeks.

Talks over a new deal at Real were at an impasse but the Spanish side have now made a new offer to Vinicius, who is understood to be appreciative of the fresh terms.

Real now await Vinicius' decision, but senior managers - including returning head coach Jose Mourinho - are now hopeful he will renew.

It is understood Real are expecting a response within hours rather than days.

If Vinicius rejects the contract, Arsenal are willing to accelerate their interest in the Brazilian.

Vinicius signed a contract extension at Real three years ago which runs until 2027, and the club and his representatives have been in talks over a fresh deal for the past 18 months.

He returned to the club on Monday for his first pre-season training session and medical assessment following his World Cup campaign with Brazil.

Vinicius, who has made 375 appearances for Real in all competitions, scoring 128 goals, is believed to want recognition as Los Blancos' top star financially.

However, Real are traditionally strict about maintaining their salary structure under president Florentino Perez.

Vinicius has publicly described Real as "the club of my dreams" and said he hopes to remain there "for many years".

Arsenal have identified the Brazilian as their priority left-wing target should his position change.

title: Newcastle appoint Jaissle - what should fans expect?
description: Newcastle United appoint Matthias Jaissle, 38, as head coach to succeed Eddie Howe - but what will the German bring to the club?
fullText:
Matthias Jaissle has quite an act to follow at Newcastle United.

"It won't be easy to succeed Eddie [Howe]," a source said.

Just like Newcastle's moves to sign young players from the continent, there is an element of risk with this appointment as the club bring in a manager who has never coached in the Premier League before.

German Jaissle delivered success in Saudi Arabia and Austria - with Al-Ahli and Red Bull Salzburg respectively - but this will be the first time he has sampled life in one of Europe's top five leagues.

He becomes the Premier League's second-youngest current head coach, at 38, and his first competitive game is against Liverpool on Sunday, 23 August.

In the statement announcing his appointment on Wednesday, Jaissle said it was an "incredible honour" to become head coach of "one of the biggest clubs in European football".

"My teams are built on togetherness, hard work, intensity and a passion to improve every single day," he added.

"I believe there is enormous potential within this squad and throughout the football club.

"I give my complete commitment and total energy to bringing further success to Newcastle United."

There has been no time to waste since Jaissle arrived at Newcastle's pre-season training camp in Spain at the weekend.

"He will try to understand the culture, what Newcastle means to the community, as soon as possible," added a source.

Howe certainly set the standard.

The Englishman took charge of a side in relegation trouble, kept them up, then went on to end Newcastle's long wait for silverware by winning the EFL Cup in 2025 - and also qualified for the Champions League on multiple occasions.

However, last season was a bruising one domestically - Newcastle finished in 12th place - and Howe watched Alexander Isak, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon leave within a year.

Newcastle are set to lose a fourth key player too, with captain Bruno Guimaraes heading to Arsenal.

They need a progressive manager to start a new cycle following Howe's decision to step down - and build on what he did at the peak of his reign.

Effectively, Jaissle's remit will be to develop players and outperform clubs with bigger wage bills. And Newcastle's squad should expect him to be just as demanding as his predecessor in training.

"We did lots of small-sided games to keep the intensity high and if someone had not been giving it their all, he called them out on it," said former Salzburg midfielder Zlatko Junuzovic.

"He's not afraid to address things head-on."

Jaissle has quickly had to get to know a new set of players, but he will encounter a group who are already used to similar principles from their time under Howe, as well as new young signings who are eager to learn.

He also brings with him a group of coaches and analysts who will look to quickly get his message across.

Al-Ahli defender Merih Demiral knows that better than most.

"Looking forward to going to training every day was so important," he added. "They paid great attention to every detail and always made sure we were fully prepared.

"Matthias has built a really strong team around him and they played a huge role in our success."

Jaissle and his staff will be working with a squad whose average age has dropped significantly this summer.

However, the German will still rely on experienced heads such as Dan Burn and Fabian Schar in the dressing room.

Jaissle, a former defender with Hoffenheim, was a few months younger than Junuzovic when he took charge of Salzburg in 2021.

But he did not shirk in telling the midfielder he would find it difficult playing alongside the younger players in the side.

Jaissle challenged Junuzovic to improve and earn his place in the starting line-up, and "kept his word" when he did.

"He understands the players' language," the former Austria international said.

Why Arsenal are signing Newcastle captain Guimaraes

Challenging times ahead for Newcastle - Shearer

It is a little telling that Red Bull Salzburg have not won the league since Jaissle departed following his second successive triumph three years ago.

The Austrian club have not reached the Champions League knockout stage, either, since doing so for the first time ever under Jaissle in 2022, even if they were ultimately hammered 8-1 on aggregate by Bayern Munich in the last 16.

Jaissle went on to show an ability to adapt at Al-Ahli with a different profile of player, winning back-to-back Asian Champions League titles.

As much as his aggressive side pressed high, and got the ball forward quickly, they also had solid defensive foundations and no other team conceded fewer goals in the Saudi Pro League last season.

Such a balanced approach will be needed if Jaissle is to succeed in the Premier League, which is a different beast altogether, as he will soon find out.

But Newcastle's new boss will certainly back himself.

"The best way to describe him is his mentality," said Turkey international Demiral.

"Even if we were losing 2-0 or 3-0, he never lost his belief. He always believed in his players and prepared us with the same mindset in training.

"This is one of the main reasons why we managed to come back and win so many matches."

It's a very different league, and challenge, but Newcastle will hope it's a sign of things to come.

Jaissle's predecessor Howe had similar principles in terms of building a side around physical intensity, pressing and direct attacks.

The German primarily uses a high-pressing 4-4-2 when the opposition are building from the back.

Even when his teams are pushed into more of a mid-block, they have shown an impressive understanding of when to step forward and transition into a high press as a collective.

Howe's defensive tactics should align well with the Red Bull style of pressing, which could make it easier for the players to buy into Jaissle's methods.

What Howe was criticised for towards the end of his tenure was a supposed lack of adaptability.

After joining Al-Ahli, Jaissle inherited a mosaic of superstars and less experienced Saudi players - a wildly different challenge from coaching a Red Bull club with consistency and understanding in style from youth level through to the first team.

While he retained his coaching principles, he recognised the need to platform players according to their individual strengths within that framework.

The Premier League is constantly evolving, with coaches designing new counter-measures to tactics that appear to work from one week to the next.

If Jaissle is going to succeed in the Premier League, that agility will be a vital asset.

title: Buttler breaks T20 runs record in Super Giants win
description: Jos Buttler stars as Manchester Super Giants beat Welsh Fire by nine wickets in The Hundred
fullText:
The Hundred men's competition, Old Trafford

Welsh Fire 155-4 (100 balls): Short 71 (47), Salt 48 (37); Atkinson 2-12

Manchester Super Giants 161-1 (69 balls): Seifert 62* (36), Buttler 51* (20); Cook 1-20

Manchester Super Giants won by nine wickets

Jos Buttler became the all-time leading run-scorer in T20 cricket as Manchester Super Giants beat Welsh Fire by nine wickets in The Hundred.

The England white-ball great passed Kieron Pollard's record of 14,803 at Old Trafford by launching the first of three consecutive sixes off Marco Jansen.

The 35-year-old finished with 51 from 20 balls, ending the match with back-to-back sixes down the ground off Lockie Ferguson.

Buttler hit two fours and six sixes, finishing alongside Tim Seifert, who struck 62 from 36 balls as Super Giants successfully reached their target of 156 with 31 balls to spare.

Cricket statisticians include The Hundred data in T20 records, meaning Buttler now has 14,833 runs in the shortest formats.

Fire captain Phil Salt made the uncommon decision to bat after winning the toss and put on an opening partnership of 125 with Matt Short.

Salt struck 48 from 37 while Short hit 71 from 47 deliveries, with the pair combining for a total of 11 fours and five sixes.

The partnership was finally broken when Salt was caught in the deep off Josh Tongue from the 83rd ball of the innings.

His wicket was the first of four lost for 13 runs, with Short caught at long-on off Paul Walter before Jordan Cox and Tom Kohler-Cadmore also found boundary fielders off Gus Atkinson, with Fire ultimately finishing on 155-4.

Super Giants started with a strong opening partnership of their own as Seifert and Paul Walter put on 74 from 35 balls.

Walter, playing in his first match of the tournament after Aiden Markram withdrew for personal reasons, hit 37 from 18 deliveries, including a run of five consecutive boundaries off Jansen and Rachin Ravindra.

The home side managed to remove the towering opener when Ben Kellaway pulled off an excellent bit of fielding on the mid-wicket rope, throwing the ball up as he stepped over the rope and stepping back on the field to collect it.

Super Giants did not slow down and sealed a win that takes them into third, four points behind Fire in second.

In the women's competition, the visitors will be hoping to move off the bottom of the table against their sixth-placed opponents when they meet at 15:00 BST.

title: 'Pivotal moment' as Lines joins British America's Cup team
description: Jemima Lines has hailed a "pivotal moment" in her sport after she became the first woman to be selected for the British America's Cup team in 90 years.
fullText:
Jemima Lines has hailed a "pivotal moment" in her sport after she became the first British woman to be selected for an America's Cup team in 90 years.

The 29-year-old has been named in the GB1 team for next year's event, which will be the first edition in its 175-year history to require at least one woman in each five-person crew.

Phyllis Sopwith was the last British woman to race aboard a British America's Cup challenger, making appearances in 1934 and 1937.

"It has been a long time coming," Lines told BBC Sport.

"It is incredible, what a moment in history and it is just so exciting, I think it is a pivotal moment for our sport really.

"It honestly is a massive honour and quite surreal. If you had told me that growing up I wouldn't have believed it."

Lines is a former kitefoiler on the British Sailing Team and was Team GB's back-up to eventual gold medallist Ellie Aldridge at the Paris 2024 Olympics.

She has a degree in mechanical engineering, and has previously worked as a guide at Everest basecamp, scaled mountain summits and set altitude kite surfing records.

Her sense of adventure, she says, came from her late father, Ralph Crathorne, a former British special forces soldier who died in an accident on Ben Nevis earlier this year.

Asked what he would make of her selection for GB1, Lines said: "He would just absolutely love it, he was an absolute legend and an incredible adventurer.

"Every sport I have ever done, we have done as a family and that lead me to this. He lead me to this really."

The 38th America's Cup will take place in takes place in Naples, Italy, in 2027, with racing beginning in May and the final Match taking place on 10-11 July.

With her engineering background, Lines will also play a key role in the design team and help to develop the tools the GB1 crew will use on board the AC75.

She joins Bleddyn Mon, Dylan Fletcher, Ben Cornish and Andrea Tesei in the GB1 crew.

"The anticipation is massive for this one and all I can say is that coming into this team you can feel the buzz in the air," Lines said.

"It is just a place full of legends, from the sailors to everyone working here. There is that daily drive and there is no waiting around.

"I think the team as a whole is expectational and I don't really want to give the game away.

"It is a design challenge first off, then you take it to the water and that is the exciting thing that the race has already started and the rest is yet to come."

title: Sprinting for GB - two years after taking up sport
description: Gloucester sprinter James Arminio is racing at the Under-20 World Championships, only two years after first stepping on to an athletics track.
fullText:
Barely two years after he first stepped on to a sprinting track, Gloucestershire teenager James Arminio will compete for Great Britain at this week's Under-20 World Championships in Oregon.

The 18-year-old, who is due to collect his A-Level results when he returns from the USA, is competing in the 4x100m relay and 100m.

"It's all happened really quickly so it's been a lot to take on whilst juggling A-Levels at the same time," Arminio told BBC Radio Gloucestershire.

"But I still have so much more to learn, I'm still new to the sport, I'm nowhere near where I need to be in terms of what I've learned. There's still much more improvement there, so much more gains to make."

It was only when Arminio started sixth form in 2024 he first got a taste of athletics, having previously played football which he says he "never took too seriously".

"My coaches always knew I was quick but it wasn't until I started track that I knew how quick I could be," he said.

Through his school he was invited to compete against other athletes from the county and eventually qualified for a regional championships.

From there, he joined Gloucester Athletics Club and linked up with his now coach Justin Smith.

Since starting consistent training, Arminio's sprint times have improved markedly and he represented Great Britain for the first time earlier this summer.

"Constantly seeing improvements, it just gives you that motivation - you're constantly seeing the times decrease, you know that if you keep doing the work that's going to keep happening," he said.

"At the start of this season, me and Justin had a chat and said the [U20] World Championships is at the end of this year, do we want to go for it? And I said 'absolutely'.

"That was the main motivation for me this season, I knew that was where I wanted to go, that was how much quicker I wanted to be."

Arminio says he is not looking too far ahead and hopes this week's competition in Eugene will be another step in his development, with his career still in its infancy.

"It would be nice to win obviously but with the level of competition it's going to take a lot to do well there," he added.

"I'm hoping to just get a good personal best, enjoy the experience, meet people and learn from them - take that into the future and grow from there."

title: Will Max Verstappen leave Red Bull? Could Fernando Alonso retire? F1’s biggest ‘silly season’ rumours
description: Four-time F1 world champion Verstappen is being heavily linked with a big-money move to Mercedes or McLaren
fullText:
Max Verstappen's future has been the topic of heated conversation for well over 18 months now, dating back to his last Formula 1 world championship triumph in 2024.

The four-time world champion, the outstanding driver of his generation, officially has a £50m-a-year contract with Red Bull until the end of the 2028 season.

However, the Dutchman is motivated by competitiveness. Red Bull have been unable to provide him with a top-tier car in the last two seasons, as illustrated by their constructors' finishing spot: third last year and, at the 2026 summer break, fourth this year. As such, Verstappen is being linked with a move away.

There is other "silly season" speculation too: Carlos Sainz is understandably disappointed with Williams' poor start to the season and is said to be looking elsewhere, while Fernando Alonso looks to be on the brink of retirement given Aston Martin's torrid plight.

Here's a round-up of the main F1 transfer stories

It is the million-dollar (or several million-dollar) question – and would have big ramifications for the rest of the grid.

Verstappen is yet to confirm his future will be at Red Bull in 2027 and, despite some post-race reactions to the contrary, the 28-year-old does look set to continue in the sport in spite of his protestations about this controversial generation of car.

The Dutchman has an exit clause in his contract allowing him to leave if he's outside the top two in the drivers' championship by the summer break – and he's currently positioned a lowly sixth in the standings, 110 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli.

But where would he go? Naturally, runaway leaders Mercedes seem the most obvious destination, given team principal Toto Wolff's previous flirtations with the Red Bull driver. Photos of Wolff holidaying with Verstappen and their families in Sardinia have only accentuated those rumours.

Yet Wolff has publicly stated how happy he is with his driver pairing. Antonelli, at 19, is the next big hotshot in the sport while Russell has publicly insisted he will still be with the team next year.

McLaren look to be the other viable option. Verstappen's trusted race engineer Ginapiero Lambiase joins the papaya as head of racing, perhaps as early as next year, and talks took place with the Dutchman's agent Raymond Vermeulen in June.

Yet the reigning world champions have struggled for consistency themselves this season, though they did earn a breakthrough win in Hungary through Lando Norris.

If Verstappen were to land a spot at the Woking-based squad, it seems highly likely that Oscar Piastri would be the one to make way… perhaps in a straight swap with Red Bull?

On the flip side, Verstappen has spoken in depth about his loyalty to Red Bull after more than 12 years in their programme. A year ago, he decided to stay put; he may well do the same this time around.

Alongside Aston Martin, Williams have been the big let-down of 2026.

James Vowles spoke in depth in the past few years about all his focus being on this year's car and, armed with the strongest engine (Mercedes), their chassis and reliability have been underwhelming.

After 11 rounds, Sainz has just six points to his name. And the Spaniard, who joined amid much hope of a Williams renaissance last year, is looking elsewhere.

He has been linked with a return to Alpine, having originally turned them down for Williams in the summer of 2024. Sainz drove for Renault for one solitary season in 2018.

The 31-year-old could also be a prime contender to swoop in if there's a big shift (ie Verstappen) further up the grid, whether it be a return to Red Bull (where he started his career in 2015 with sister team Toro Rosso) or otherwise.

The knock-on impact of a Sainz departure would be big, too: it could mean Franco Colapinto returns to the team from Alpine. Again, a straight swap could materialise.

This question may well be the first we get answered after the summer break.

The 45-year-old acknowledged that he will spend his three-week holiday contemplating his future in the sport, after what has been a disastrous start to the season for Aston Martin and their new engine partner Honda.

It seems very unlikely that Alonso will switch teams for 2027. The question really is: does he have faith in Adrian Newey to turn the team's form around for next year – and significantly enough that he can challenge right at the top?

The slowest team on the grid for much of the campaign so far, they have some way to go at this stage.

title: Derry City part ways with manager Lynch
description: Tiernan Lynch has left his position as Derry City manager by mutual consent after a poor run of form.
fullText:
Tiernan Lynch has left his position as Derry City manager by mutual consent after a poor run of form.

The Candystripes sit sixth in the Premier Division and have won just one of their past seven games.

The 50-year-old joined the side on a three-year deal in November 2024 from Larne, who won back-to-back Irish Premiership titles during his tenure.

"The club would like to place on record its sincere thanks to Tiernan for his professionalism, commitment and hard work during his time at Derry City," the club posted on social media following the news.

Despite making big signings such as former Republic of Ireland international James McClean during the off season, Derry have struggled to build on last season's second-place finish.

McClean has also since voiced his concerns since joining the club and said there was 'issue somewhere' at Derry City after they exited the Uefa Conference League at the second qualifying round.

The club have confirmed that Mark Connolly will become interim manager and is due to be in the dugout when Derry face Sligo on Friday, 7 August - a game to be shown live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport NI website.

An appointment that generated so much excitement but ultimately failed to deliver has come to an end.

After the impressive job Lynch did with the Inver Reds, there were high expectations for what he and his brother Seamus could achieve at the Ryan McBride Brandywell Stadium and a belief they could deliver the silverware the club so crave.

Finishing just three points behind champions Shamrock Rovers and securing European football was considered a successful debut season for Lynch.

Expectations only grew for his second season after more high-profile signings including former Sunderland and Wrexham player McClean.

From the start of the season, however, it was clear the side were not building upon the previous campaign as they registered just nine points from their first 10 games.

The club's struggles continued on the European stage and they lost to CSKA Sofia in the Europa League qualifiers before being knocked out of the Conference League qualifiers by Rijeka following another lacklustre display - it was after the latter that Lynch said his players needed to be "braver".

As frustrations grew, injuries to key players such as Liam Boyce left the side short of attacking options for significant periods too.

Growing tensions around the squad have been evident and the outspoken McClean's social media posts of recent days when he spoke of "issues" at the club can only have created more friction.

While we will never know the true level of divide between the manager and the players, the relationship between both sides seemed increasingly strained and makes news of Lynch's departure less of a surprise.

It will be a tough task for whoever takes over to steady the ship this season.

Already 14 points behind the top three with 10 games to go, it looks highly unlikely that the club can secure European football through their league position.

However, the new manager will still have the potential of the FAI Cup to try and salvage something from this increasingly lost campaign.

title: Briton Chapman suffers brain bleed after sparring session
description: British boxer Raven Chapman was airlifted to hospital and placed in a medically induced coma after suffering a brain bleed following a sparring session in Denmark on 24 July.
fullText:
British boxer Raven Chapman was airlifted to hospital and placed in a medically induced coma after suffering a brain bleed following a sparring session in Denmark on 24 July.

The 32-year-old former world title challenger collapsed after training and was taken by helicopter to hospital, where she was diagnosed with a brain haematoma and cerebral oedema.

Her management company, Vote Boxing, said Chapman underwent emergency surgery to stop the bleeding and reduce the swelling before being placed in a medically induced coma.

"Over the past day, she has been taken off the sedatives and is continuing to receive treatment while awaiting medically supervised repatriation to a hospital in the UK, where her rehabilitation is expected to take some time," the statement said.

Chapman has won 10 professional fights with two losses.

The Norwich-born fighter lost to Skye Nicolson for the WBC featherweight title in October 2024 in the only women's world-title fight ever to be held in Saudi Arabia.

Vote Boxing said Chapman's doctors were "doing everything they can to support her recovery" and that they remained "hopeful as she continues to fight through this incredibly difficult time".

The statement added that Chapman's family are with her in Denmark.

A GoFundMe page has been launched to help raise funds, while messages of support have poured in from across the boxing community, including former promoter Frank Warren.

"Raven is fully in my thoughts this morning. I'm really hoping she can pull through and get home safely. Everyone at Queensberry is behind you, Raven. We're all hoping you can pull through this," Warren wrote on X.

Japanese winger Daisuke Yokota hopes to make "special memories" after joining Rangers from Hannover.

Yokota, 26, has joined on a three-year deal with the option of an additional year and becomes the Ibrox side's ninth summer signing.

He moved to Germany as a teenager and spent time with FSV Frankfurt and Carl Zeiss Jena before stints in Latvia with Valmiera and in Poland with Gornik Zabrze.

A move to Belgian side Gent followed in 2024, but Yokota was unable to establish himself in the first team and was loaned to Kaiserslautern and Hannover.

Hannover signed him permanently earlier this summer off the back of five goals and four assists in the German second tier.

"I'm really excited to be joining Rangers," Yokota told club media. "This is a massive club with a fantastic history, passionate supporters and high ambitions so it's a proud moment for me.

"My aim is to help the team achieve success this season and I hope we can create some special memories together."

What did Premiership start tell us about Scottish sides' Euro hopes?

Dundee Utd hold Rangers in Premiership opener

Same start but different outlook at Rangers as McInnes era begins

Djeidi Gassama and on-loan Tottenham player Mikey Moore were Rangers' main wide options last season but Moore has since returned to his parent club.

Findlay Curtis is back at Rangers after a spell on loan at Kilmarnock and replaced Gassama in Friday's Scottish Premiership-opening 1-1 draw at Dundee United.

And manager Derek McInnes said: "Daisuke is a player we have been aware of for some time and he brings qualities that we believe will really strengthen our attacking options.

"At 26, he has gained valuable experience across a number of different leagues in Europe. He is quick, direct and has the ability to make things happen in the final third.

"We are continuing to strengthen the squad in key areas."

The deal for Yokota is subject to international clearance and visa and Rangers have not confirmed whether he will be available for Thursday's Europa League third qualifying round tie first leg with Jagiellonia Bialystok in Poland.

title: Prendergast takes four as Fire beat Super Giants
description: Ireland international Orla Prendergast takes 4-18 as Welsh Fire beat Manchester Super Giants by three wickets at Old Trafford.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, Old Trafford

Manchester Super Giants 85-9 (100 balls): MacDonald-Gay 18* (14); Prendergast 4-18

Welsh Fire (91 balls): Wareham 17 (12); Ecclestone 3-14

Welsh Fire won by three wickets

Ireland international Orla Prendergast took 4-18 as Welsh Fire beat Manchester Super Giants by three wickets at Old Trafford.

Playing only her second Hundred match after arriving as an injury replacement for Sophie Devine, the seamer tore through the Super Giants' top-order as the hosts slipped to 24-4.

Prendergast bowled Super Giants captain Meg Lanning for a golden duck, had Mady Villiers caught for five and then trapped Kathryn Bryce (4) lbw, before Heather Graham had Paige Scholfield (5) stumped.

India's Smriti Mandhana made 15 before she was run-out after being called through for a risky single, while Sophie Ecclestone (9) became Graham's second stumping victim.

Richa Ghosh was Prendergast's fourth wicket, caught in the covers for 11, but Ryana MacDonald-Gay top-scored from number nine, hitting an unbeaten 18 to help her side reach 85-9.

Fire reached 27 in their reply, before losing Sarah Bryce, caught and bowled by Bex Tyson for 16, while fellow opener Georgia Voll reached the same score before skying a catch off Villiers.

Ecclestone removed Freya Kemp (6) and Prendergast with successive balls, having her England team-mate clip to Lanning at short mid-on and then bowling the Ireland all-rounder. She also had Georgia Wareham caught well by Lanning for 17 in her figures of 3-14.

Graham guided Fire to a nervy victory, losing two further partners but hitting an unbeaten 16, including the winning runs as her side reached 88-7 with nine balls to spare.

The win moved Fire above Leeds Sunrisers into fourth place and two points behind Super Giants who remain third.

title: TV presenter Knowles buys stake in Cornish Pirates
description: Television presenter Nick Knowles becomes a shareholder in Champ Rugby side Cornish Pirates.
fullText:
Television presenter Nick Knowles has become a shareholder in Champ Rugby side Cornish Pirates.

The presenter, best known for shows such as DIY SOS and National Lottery: Who Dares Wins, is the latest person to join the club's ownership group.

Pirates became the first English professional side to have American ownership when Pittsburgh-based Stonewood Capital Management took a stake in May.

"He's Cornish by choice," Cornish Pirates chief executive Sally Pettipher told BBC Sport.

"There's a spirit to the place that gets under your skin and he's been an ambassador for Cornish Pirates for over a season now already, he's in the crowd and people don't know.

"This investment, becoming a shareholder, is him putting some skin in the game and bringing with him his rugby heritage.

"He's got a rugby brain, he's got a rugby background, he's well connected in that world, he does an awful lot of philanthropy in that world and he brings visibility to us, which I think is really important.

"So the more eyes on we have, the more we can build our national and international audience.

"He is talented beyond what you see on screen and I'm very, very grateful for his input."

Cornish Pirates secure 'landmark' US investment

Local consortium takes over at Cornish Pirates

The club has been looking for more investment since long-serving owner Sir Dicky Evans' near three-decade association with the club ended in January 2025.

Cornish Pirates' ownership is now a mix of their United States-based investors and a group of shareholders based closer to home.

"That's an enabling investment to take us to the stage after this," added Pettipher.

"So it's important, but it's not a lottery win, I would say.

"We have a 10-year development plan. If I can make it faster I will, but the 10-year development plan is a series of investments that gets us to be a top of Premiership club.

"That's a long way from where we are because we have to be ready, have to meet minimum standards, and we have to be a fantastic Championship club."

While the lack of a suitable stadium that meets Prem Rugby criteria could be seen as the club's biggest obstacle to promotion to the Prem under the new franchise-based system, Pettipher says there are other equally as big hurdles:

"There are many minimum standards that are required to become a Premiership club and one of those is a business plan that allows you to commercially exist," she said.

"There's a new minimum standard that's come in which is a salary floor, so not just a salary cap. So the business plan has to support a £5m budget for your rugby players alone.

"People don't think about the fact that we only have 14 trading days a year, 14 home matches.

"So actually, what we have to do as a business is create a business that is working 365 days a year and is generating the sort of income that can support a club with a business plan required by the Premiership.

"The great thing about these new investors is they are very, very talented business people as well as rugby people.

"So adding in business brains and planning brains and information networks and contact networks is a gift that they give and an investment that they're putting in alongside the financials."

Meanwhile, work on the new main grandstand at the Mennaye will not be ready in time for Cornish Pirates' pre-season game with Saracens on 28 August.

The structure was badly hit during Storm Goretti in early January, with part of the roof blown off and structural damage caused.

It led to the club having to play two league matches at nearby Camborne while work was done to make the Mennaye safe.

"The painful thing is that that stand is not going to be ready for us when we play Saracens at the end of this month," added Pettipher.

"The grandstand will be a building site and unavailable, which is extremely upsetting to me because that is 600 premium seats that we are unable to use and that hits my bottom line quite substantially.

"It should be ready for our first league match which is on 20 September."

title: Heavyweight Parker cleared to fight after drugs ban
description: Former world heavyweight champion Joseph Parker has been cleared to fight again after his provisional suspension for testing positive for cocaine was lifted.
fullText:
Former world heavyweight champion Joseph Parker has been cleared to fight again after his provisional suspension for testing positive for cocaine was lifted.

The 34-year-old New Zealander was tested by the Voluntary Anti-Doping Association (Vada) on 25 October.

On the same day, he was beaten by Britain's Fabio Wardley at London's O2 Arena.

"I'm pleased to confirm my provisional suspension is lifted and I'll be back in the ring soon," Parker said on Wednesday.

"I've been advised to say no more for now while details are finalised. Thank you to all my supporters."

Parker has denied knowingly taking any banned substances. He had faced the possibility of a ban of up to two years, with any sanction to be determined by UK Anti-Doping (Ukad) and the British Boxing Board of Control (BBBoC).

The BBBoC confirmed to BBC Sport that Parker's provisional suspension has been lifted but said it "cannot make any further comment at this stage".

BBC Sport has also contacted Ukad, which did not oversee the original test and would need to carry out its own investigation.

Parker holds a professional record of 36 wins and four defeats. He was WBO heavyweight champion from 2016 to 2018 before losing the title to Britain's Anthony Joshua in Cardiff.

Newly promoted Hull City have signed Greece goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis from Olympiacos for a club record fee.

description: Officials at the Tour de France Femmes Avec Zwift will check the clothing worn by riders to prevent attempts to make "aerodynamic gains".
fullText:
Riders at the Tour de France Femmes Avec Zwift have had their clothing checked to prevent attempts to make "aerodynamic gains".

Issues have reportedly been raised about padding in bras that could result in riders gaining one second per kilometre.

Race organiser ASO issued a statement following Dutch media reports of concerns some riders had used bra padding as aerodynamic fairings to improve efficiency.

Other items have also been known to be inserted into a skinsuit around the chest area to smooth airflow around the body.

"Riders must be to the final checks before the race (bikes and outfit) no later than 10 minutes before their respective start time," the statement said.

"Particular attention will be paid to compliance with article 1.3.032 of the UCI regulations, including non-essential elements and clothing or other items/accessories worn by a rider (including but not limited to helmets, glasses, shoes or in-race communication devices) which could modify riders' morphology."

Dutch outlet Wielerflits, external said the practice had been seen previously in women's cycling, including at the Paris 2024 Olympics.

Riders could face disqualification from a race and a fine of nearly £200.

Reusser takes Tour lead with time trial win

Much attention is paid to airflow and aerodynamic efficiency in cycling as the correct shape of bike frame and skinsuit can save a rider several seconds, especially during a time trial - where a rider races alone against the clock.

In ski jumping last February, male athletes were accused of using penis injections to aid aerodynamic efficiency.

Cycling's world governing body the UCI's rule also says it prohibits clothing "not strictly necessary for the functionality of the clothing, or other item, or accessory".

"The problem is how are you going to police it?" Lidl-Trek's head of technical and innovation, Koen de Kort, told The Athletic., external

"That's the biggest issue. You can say it's not allowed [but] how can you say how much a woman needs?

"That's time to get pretty much into a grey area of what you're allowed to check."

In a study by researchers at universities in Scotland and the Netherlands, a mannequin of a male rider, 177cm in height, inside a wind tunnel found fairings can give rise to "significant drag aero reductions" and that wider objects yielded the largest gains.

title: Transfer 'shark' De Zerbi hopes to drag Spurs up from depths
description: Through his self-confessed love of the transfer window, Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi hopes he can guide his club back up the Premier League table.
fullText:
There was a moment last season when Roberto de Zerbi turned to his Tottenham players and asked: "Did we pass away?"

The scenes after his first game in charge - a 1-0 defeat at Sunderland - painted a grim picture.

In the dressing room, De Zerbi said players were lying on their backs, some crying following the loss at the Stadium of Light.

It was the first of seven matches De Zerbi had to keep Spurs in the Premier League.

While survival was only secured on the final day, the 47-year-old now believes he can help the club rise from the ignominy of a turbulent 2025-26 campaign.

Four months on from the broken dressing room in Sunderland, the contrast is stark.

At the team's hotel in Sydney for their pre-season tour, just a stone's throw from the Harbour Bridge and iconic Opera House, De Zerbi's players are laughing, smiling and enjoying coffees made by their own barista on a private floor.

Competitive table tennis matches are taking place as a club-record £237m worth of new signings integrate into a squad dreaming of a return to the upper echelons of English football and a renewed challenge for trophies.

Club-record signing Sandro Tonali, plus new arrivals Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke, Andrew Robertson and Martin Dubravka have all featured on Spurs' pre-season tour.

After featuring for Argentina in the World Cup final, Marcos Senesi was granted extended leave and is the only new recruit not to have featured in Australia and New Zealand, but has now begun training at Hotspur Way.

"I deserve to want the top players, because now Tottenham deserves to build up a top team," De Zerbi said.

It was an unusual position for Spurs, but they had two transfer plans: one for relegation and one for survival.

De Zerbi, who reiterates he would have continued managing Spurs in the Championship, is happy to be working from Plan A, including "respecting the will" of players such as club captain Cristian Romero and goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario, who could yet leave.

"At the beginning of my time in April I had one million individual meetings," he jokes. "They told me if they didn't want to be here. I said: 'Yes, help me to stay up, and then I help you to leave.

"'If you don't help me to stay up, you stay underwater with me'."

Spurs have undergone radical change over the past 12 months amid understandable fan anger, with new chief executive Vinai Venkatesham leading the organisation on behalf of the Lewis Family Trust.

Venkatesham, alongside technical director Johan Lange, is leading negotiations. Lange is the only senior figure from the previous regime to remain in post.

They are supported by director of football operations Rafi Moersen and new performance director Dan Lewindon, both of whom arrived from Manchester City's parent company, City Football Group.

Lewindon has been tasked with improving Spurs' injury record.

But De Zerbi is hands on in all areas of the club and says "in the transfer market, when I want one player, I become like a shark.

That approach has helped secure record deals for £85m Fernandes from West Ham and £100m Tonali from Newcastle.

"I love working in the transfer market. It's not a pressure, it's one of the nicest parts in my work, in my job," he explained.

But where does that enjoyment come from?

"I don't know, maybe because when you take the decision, you take the responsibility. If the coach calls the player, you can build a special connection at the beginning.

"With Mateus Fernandes, I spoke with the mum, with the father."

De Zerbi told Fernandes' father that he would be his "second dad" and look after him in England.

Spurs also signed defender Van Hecke despite reported interest from Chelsea, having already beaten Manchester United and Manchester City to the two record-breaking midfielders.

Transfers are a world of game theory. Insiders have told BBC Sport that Spurs knew they had to be both aggressive and quick, with the first quality likely extending to fees, wages and De Zerbi's personal involvement in courting players.

After the 2-2 draw with Brighton in April, in which Georginio Rutter scored a 95th-minute equaliser to dent Spurs' survival hopes, De Zerbi revealed he messaged Van Hecke, who assisted the goal.

"You wanted to push down Tottenham for Brighton when you made the assist to Rutter, now you have to come to me, you have no choice," De Zerbi revealed.

For Tonali, De Zerbi detailed how he texted him the day after Spurs secured their Premier League status with a final-day win over Everton, before meeting him at his home in Brescia in what proved to be a decisive conversation.

Club staff then completed the deal following several further discussions.

Now he is teasing what he calls a final attacking "bomba", with moves for two forwards expected, including one for Manchester City's Savinho.

De Zerbi believes it would be wrong to suggest Spurs are spending irresponsibly.

He said he is under "no pressure" despite the Lewis family injecting £100m into the club in June because it was desperately needed, arguing that Chelsea, Arsenal and Liverpool have all done the same in recent years.

There have also been departures, with the club earning substantial fee for Luka Vuskovic's £45m move to Brighton. Doubts remain over the futures of midfielder Lucas Bergvall and England full-back Djed Spence.

"We assessed the request of Vuskovic [to join Brighton], with Vinai, with Johan together, because I consider Tottenham's money my money," De Zerbi said.

"It's like the owner is my father, I think you don't want to ask your father to lose money.

"Like all the big clubs, we have to sell a player at as big of a price [as possible] and we have to bring a player with a small price, we are starting for a plan of five seasons because we are building."

There was also the disciplined decision not to sign Joao Palhinha on a permanent transfer from Bayern Munich, not because De Zerbi felt he was not good enough, but because the overall financial package was not considered suitable.

After the Sunderland game, there was also a sense of sadness and negativity among staff at the training ground.

"The day after I organised a meeting without players and I said, 'The first one I see say something negative, I send you home immediately'," said De Zerbi.

It is now about changing the "behaviour, attitude and spirit" of those at Spurs who suffered that traumatic season, having also finished 17th the previous campaign, albeit without the same fear of relegation and with a Europa League triumph under Ange Postecoglou.

He explains that he took his players for "one big dinner in Mayfair, with alcohol" and believes Spurs were unfortunate in their final matches and could have secured survival sooner.

"I think they considered themselves in that moment worse than the people thought," De Zerbi admits, adding that the healing process continues. "I hope next time they organise [dinner and drinks] for themselves.

"With love, friendship and care, you become top, top, top."

title: Salah mobbed at airport before Trabzonspor move
description: Turkish club Trabzonspor are set to confirm the signing of Egypt captain and former Liverpool forward Mohamed Salah.
fullText:
Turkish club Trabzonspor are set to confirm the signing of Mohamed Salah as the Egypt captain was mobbed by fans on his arrival in Turkey.

Hundreds of fans gathered outside Ataturk Airport in Istanbul on Wednesday as Salah emerged wearing Trabzonspor colours before engaging with the excited crowd.

The 34-year-old forward left Liverpool at the end of last season after nine years on Merseyside, scoring 257 goals.

It is unclear what Salah will earn at Trabzonspor, but as he is a free agent, the Super Lig club will have been able to commit more of their budget towards Salah's wages.

Salah, who has scored 50 Champions League goals, will play European football with Trabzonspor next season after they finished third, eight points behind champions Galatasaray.

If they fail to progress to the league phase of the Europa League via the play-offs, they will drop down to the Conference League.

Salah became Liverpool's highest earner in their history when he signed a reported £400,000-a-week contract in April 2025.

Nicknamed the Black Sea Storm, Trabzonspor have won seven league titles, six of which came between 1976 and 1984.

In 2022, they claimed their most recent league success, ending a 38-year wait.

Based in the north-eastern city of Trabzon, they are one of only six teams to have won the Turkish Super Lig.

Salah's signing will go down as the club's biggest as he joins former Liverpool striker Daniel Sturridge and former Arsenal winger Nicolas Pepe in donning the claret and sky blue shirt.

He helped the Liverpool to win two Premier League titles, the Champions League, the Club World Cup, Uefa Super Cup, FA Cup and two EFL Cups.

During his time in England, the Egyptian won the Premier League Golden Boot on four occasions and was named the Professional Footballers' Association player of the year three times - in 2018, 2022 and 2025.

But despite scoring 29 goals and making 18 assists in Liverpool's 2024-25 title-winning season, Salah's minutes diminished the following campaign after a falling out with former Reds head coach Arne Slot.

Since announcing he would be leaving Liverpool a year before his two-year contract extension ended, the football world has been wondering where he would next be playing.

After a successful World Cup campaign where Egypt reached the round of 16 for the first time before narrowly losing to Argentina, Salah was reported to be close to an agreement with a different Turkish club, Besiktas.

With a deal breaking down reportedly because of finances, Salah reached an agreement instead with Trabzonspor.

The Turkish side took to their social media on Tuesday night to tease the arrival of Salah with the Pyramids being shown on a video next to Papara Park.

But, following swiftly was another post stating "negotiations had begun" between Salah and Trabzonspor before showing how Salah's Wednesday flight into Istanbul could be tracked.

"Trabzon, are you ready? See you very soon," he said in a video onboard a private jet and posted on social media.

Trabzonpor's flight tracking came in handy as a huge amount of fans gathered outside the airport to welcome Salah, who was greeted like a movie star.

As one of sport's biggest global stars, this transfer for Trabzonspor is huge.

Their current squad includes on-loan Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana, as well as a couple of Cape Verde's World Cup stars in Wagner Pina and Sidny Lopes Cabral.

There can be little doubt that Trabzonspor have completed one of the biggest transfers in Turkish football history.

The country is no stranger to global stars: Roberto Carlos, Didier Drogba, Robin van Persie, Samuel Eto'o, Mesut Ozil and Wesley Sneijder have all played in the Super Lig.

This season, supporters will be able to watch N'Golo Kante and Ederson at Fenerbahce; Victor Osimhen, Ilkay Gundogan and Leroy Sane at Galatasaray; and now Salah at Trabzonspor.

A transfer of this magnitude however represents a significant departure for Trabzonspor who, while competing for the title, have focused on developing young players and identifying talent with resale potential.

With the league increasingly dominated by Fenerbahce and Galatasaray, enthusiasm among Trabzonspor supporters had appeared to fade and Papara Park was often below capacity.

The signing of Salah is an attempt to change that.

His arrival should bring supporters back and significantly increase shirt sales. It could also broaden Trabzonspor's commercial appeal across the Middle East, while generating particular interest among the Arab community in Trabzon and visitors to the city.

It is a bold change in strategy for Trabzonspor and Salah offers a renewed sense of excitement.

title: Key questions as Infantino faces Fifa executives
description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino will face senior leaders of football's world governing body on Wednesday. This is what is expected to happen.
fullText:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino will meet with senior leaders of football's world governing body on Wednesday as criticism of his now scrapped plan to sell off Fifa's commercial and event operations intensifies.

After secretary general Mattias Grafstrom sent a highly critical internal memo to Fifa staff, Infantino summoned members of the Fifa management board to Morocco.

Tuesday also saw chief of global football development Arsene Wenger insist he was "not involved" in Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, adding that aborting it was "absolutely necessary and beyond question".

Prince Ali, president of the Jordanian Football Association, then accused Fifa of creating a situation which "amounts to blackmail" over unpaid prize money and support for Infantino's re-election.

These claims have not been verified by the BBC, and Fifa made no comment when approached. But Prince Ali's statement is indicative of the strength of feeling among the member associations that oppose Infantino.

At the weekend, Uefa said it had lost confidence in Infantino's leadership. Several member associations - including Wales, with England set to follow suit - have withdrawn support for his re-election.

Now Infantino will meet with Fifa's hierarchy to try to secure his position.

BBC Sport understands the meeting will take place at Fifa's Africa office in Rabat.

It will include Grafstrom and members of the Fifa management board.

Among those in attendance will be finance chief Thomas Peyer, legal chief Emilio Garcia Silvero, chief of staff Daniel O'Toole, chief of member associations Elkhan Mammadov and media relations director Bryan Swanson.

It is unclear the intention of the meeting, but it is expected that Infantino will attempt to build bridges in an attempt to create a path to remaining as president.

However, this may not be straightforward.

In his letter to Fifa staff, Grafstrom said the events of the past week had been "a sad and reproachable series of events" which were "difficult to comprehend and accept".

On Friday, Kevin Lamour, Fifa's chief operating officer, said the private investment plan was "the project of one person". He added Fifa's own administration was "deceived".

Infantino will have to show contrition and perhaps offer a route to reform if he is to win back the support of his inner circle.

Carlos Cordeiro, Infantino's senior adviser on global strategy and governance, quit on Friday over the plan.

Cordeiro said the proposal was "a bad deal for football" and would "mortgage football's future".

Member associations had been given a deadline of 19 September to approve the plan or miss out on the extra funding that came as part of the deal.

In his resignation announcement, Cordeiro offered a series of questions which Infantino will likely face at Wednesday's meeting.

"Most troubling of all," Mr Cordeiro said, "is the absence of answers to fundamental questions.

"Why this deal? Why now? What oversight exists? Who benefits? Was there a competitive process? What governance will be in place? What will investors ultimately gain, and at what cost to football?

"These questions remain largely unanswered, and yet member associations are being asked to make a decision of enormous consequence in barely 50 days or risk being left behind.

"That is not a responsible way to determine the future of the world's game.

"This proposal has become a defining question for Fifa's future."

On top of this, Infantino may also have to map out - or could offer - a route for reform.

This may involve putting additional checks and balances in place that would make it impossible for such a plan to be devised and presented in this way again.

Perhaps he could shelve his plans for a 64-team World Cup? Or offer to open up Fifa's cash reserves?

Courting controversy and befriending Trump - the story of Fifa boss Infantino

Infantino calls executive meeting as criticism mounts

Infantino opponents threaten 'non co-operation' with Fifa

It seems unlikely that Infantino will leave his position as Fifa president by the end of Wednesday.

Infantino has, so far, shown no indication he is considering relinquishing his position. Indeed, he has been trying to rally his core supporter base around the globe.

On Tuesday we saw African countries Egypt, Morocco, Niger, Mauritania and DR Congo all issue statements in support of Infantino.

Infantino will, however, have to answer serious questions about a hugely controversial and damaging week for Fifa.

There may be those in the room who will query his ability to turn this around, especially with such fierce criticism from European countries.

Could that criticism be strong enough for Infantino to tender his resignation?

More likely, perhaps, Infantino could see this as the start of the fightback.

We may see a statement that will include an apology and a promise of change.

If Infantino does vow to fight on, Uefa and countries from other confederations must look to find other ways to oust him.

The Fifa Council could try to force Infantino's hand through an emergency meeting.

Such a gathering would be triggered if 19 of the 37 Fifa Council members call for one.

However, BBC Sport understands there are doubts that the 19 votes could be achieved.

Another step could be an extraordinary congress of the 211 Fifa member associations, which would be held if one-fifth, or 43 associations, "make such a request in writing".

So Uefa, which has 55 nations, can trigger the extraordinary congress whenever it wishes.

That would take a minimum of two months from the point it is triggered, but more likely three months, and there is no guarantee of success.

In effect, it would be a de facto election without there being another candidate as 106 votes would be needed to pass the vote of no confidence.

Infantino would have time to win back votes from those who had been angered by the investment plan.

Uefa can only really go down this route if it is confident of getting over the line.

Which leaves finding a suitable candidate to fight the election at the Fifa Congress in March.

Infantino stood unopposed when he was re-elected in 2019 and 2023 and if someone wants to battle him for the position, the deadline to announce their candidacy is 18 November.

Concacaf president Victor Montagliani is seen as the most likely unity candidate to stand against Infantino.

But there should be no expectation of success. Even at the height of the Fifa scandal in 2015, Sepp Blatter was re-elected as president eight days before he eventually resigned.

If Infantino is still in position later on Wednesday, this story could yet have a long way to run.

Inside Fifa, the expectation is that Infantino has called the meeting in Rabat in an attempt to clear the air, have a show of unity and try to achieve some alignment with his senior staff.

But while that may be the beleaguered president's intention, what remains uncertain is what kind of response he will receive from those present, especially given the highly critical statements issued in recent days by chief of global football development Wenger, secretary general Grafstrom and chief operating officer Lamour.

Some staff are asking if that could have emboldened others at the top of the organisation to speak out against him or to even insist he steps down.

It is no surprise Infantino has chosen Morocco, where he has been based over the past week.

Morocco is friendly territory for him. Not only is the country hosting the next World Cup, its national football association has come out in support of him. And it is where he still hopes to be re-elected for a fourth term at next year's Congress.

The Uefa-led rebellion against him will be hoping that it does not get that far, and that he has been forced to quit long before then.
