title: Why Liverpool are ready to make Barcola third £100m signing
description: With Liverpool prepared to make Bradley Barcola their third £100m signing, BBC Sport looks at what the France and Paris St-Germain winger would bring to Anfield.
fullText:
Liverpool have twice paid more than £100m for players - midfielder Florian Wirtz and striker Alexander Isak - and could be about to pay that much once again.

Paris St-Germain and France winger Bradley Barcola has become a main target for Liverpool, with the Reds prepared to pay about £100m, while PSG are holding out for somewhere near £145m.

Liverpool, who finished fifth in the Premier League last season, 25 points behind champions Arsenal, could eventually end up paying Bayer Leverkusen £116m for Wirtz, while they shelled out a club record £125m to sign Isak from Newcastle in September.

And they could be about to break the bank yet again to bring in 23-year-old Barcola, who was part of France's squad at the World Cup.

He came on as a second-half substitute in both the past two Champions League finals, when PSG beat Inter Milan 5-0 in 2024-25 and then in May when they edged past Arsenal on penalties to retain their title.

Barcola moved to PSG from Lyon in 2023 for a reported £38.5m and has since also won three Ligue 1 titles, the French Cup twice, as well as the Uefa Super Cup and the Fifa Intercontinental Cup.

He is right footed, although he prefers to play on the left wing, but can also play on the right or through the middle.

However, with PSG also having Georgia's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and France's Desire Doue as wide options, Barcola does not play 90 minutes every match so a move to Anfield would give him more playing time.

With Mohamed Salah leaving on a free transfer at the end of last season having scored 257 goals in a hugely successful nine-year spell with the Reds, Liverpool clearly need to strengthen their attack.

France forward Hugo Ekitike ruptured his Achilles tendon in April and is not expected to play again in 2026, while Cody Gakpo, another who can play on the left and in the middle, has been linked with a move to Tottenham, although Liverpool say they do not want to sell.

The Reds' other current attacking options include 17-year-old Rio Ngumoha, Italy forward Federico Chiesa and new signing Victor Munoz.

Barcola has played 28 times for France and scored three goals in this summer's World Cup, including in the 6-4 loss to England in the third-place play-off.

However, like at club level, his game time was limited because of the skills of his 21-year-old PSG team-mate Doue.

Boss Didier Deschamps stuck with Ballon d'Or holder Ousmane Dembele on the right and rotated Barcola and Doue, with both men starting four of France's eight World Cup matches, but never in the same game.

At first glance, Barcola looks like the natural successor to Luis Diaz.

Liverpool chose not to sign a direct replacement after the Colombian's departure last summer, but the underlying data suggests the PSG forward could fill that void.

Opta's player similarity model rates the Frenchman as the winger whose output most closely resembled Diaz's across Europe's top five leagues in 2025-26 (78%), with Mohamed Salah (65%), Lamine Yamal (61%) and Vinicius Junior (61%) the next closest matches.

A closer look, however, suggests Liverpool would not simply be replacing one winger with another.

Barcola is a left winger by trade, having played almost all of his Champions League minutes for PSG on that flank, but his game is shaped by a centre-forward's instincts. He played as a striker until the age of 17, something reflected in his movement and shot selection.

Last season, he averaged 3.5 shots per 90 minutes in Ligue 1, placing him among the division's most active shooters despite operating from wide areas.

His 9.83 expected goals (xG) ranked in the 95th percentile among wingers across Europe's top five leagues, meaning only around 5% of wide players consistently found themselves in better goalscoring positions.

Barcola converted those chances into 11 league goals, outperforming his xG, while no PSG player or Ligue 1 winger recorded a higher xG total during the 2025-26 campaign.

Those instincts are reflected in how he attacks defenders. Barcola was the only player across Europe's top five leagues to average more than two shot-ending carries per 90 minutes (2.06), illustrating his ability to drive at opponents before creating shooting opportunities for himself.

He also averaged 8.69 touches in the opposition penalty area per 90 minutes - the seventh-highest figure among more than 1,500 eligible players - reinforcing the profile of a winger who consistently occupies goalscoring positions.

His shot map highlights a player who attacks dangerous central areas rather than settling for speculative efforts from distance. Only Ousmane Dembele had a better combined shot volume with chance creation in Ligue 1, underlining Barcola's rare ability to both finish attacks and create opportunities for team-mates.

The comparison with Salah is equally revealing. While both pose a significant goal threat, Barcola is a more direct ball carrier.

He attempted more take-ons per 90 than the Egypt forward last season (4.26 to 3.38), but created fewer chances (2.16 to 2.33), attempted far fewer crosses (1.15 to 4.89) and through balls (0.25 to 0.59).

The numbers point towards a player who looks to eliminate defenders himself rather than orchestrate attacks from wide areas.

There are also signs that his game continues to evolve under Luis Enrique.

Barcola's passing profile across his three Champions League campaigns at PSG has become increasingly focused on progressing play in the final third, reflecting greater tactical maturity.

Rather than dribbling at every opportunity, he now shows a better understanding of when to accelerate attacks and when to recycle possession.

His work without the ball is another reason Liverpool's recruitment team are understood to admire him. Barcola ranked ninth across Europe's top five leagues for possessions won in the final third last season, a metric that reflects the aggressive pressing and intensity likely to be demanded under Andoni Iraola.

That profile may suit Liverpool's evolving attack. With Wirtz excelling at releasing runners between the lines, and Ekitike and Isak expected to occupy central defenders, Liverpool arguably need another player capable of attacking space rather than demanding the ball to feet.

Barcola's willingness to make penetrative runs and arrive in goalscoring positions could provide exactly that.

Perhaps most encouragingly for any prospective buyer, there is reason to believe Barcola has not yet reached his ceiling.

A late physical developer, he has already transformed from a promising Lyon academy graduate into a two-time Champions League winner with PSG.

At just 23, his blend of pace, intelligent movement, elite shot volume, relentless pressing and growing creative output suggests one of Europe's most complete young wide forwards is still improving.

Lee: He's proved his worth. A big signing for the new manager makes sense, get the season started with a buzz. Realistically we still need to look at the back four conundrum though.

Stu: Barcola would be a good signing but he's not worth anywhere near £100m, never mind £145m. He's a squad player at PSG. If they won't accept £70m max then move on to someone else.

Andrew: Ridiculous amount of money. Can Barcola actually last a full 90 minutes? He seemed to be subbed between 60 and 70 mins. I hope that proves to be wrong if we buy him.

Paul: There appears to be enough attacking options already, surely last year showed the need is in defence. Make the backline solid and build out from there.

title: What happens next with Rashford and Man Utd?
description: Marcus Rashford is expected to return to Manchester United training in the coming days as debate continues over whether that is a good thing or not.
fullText:
The unlikely Manchester United reunion is close to completion.

When Marcus Rashford was unveiled by Barcelona in July 2025, at the start of a season-long loan, no-one expected he would find himself back at Old Trafford 12 months later.

United gave his coveted number 10 shirt to new arrival Matheus Cunha.

Rashford was also looking to the future as he assessed the move to Spain.

"[Manchester United] is in a period of change and have been for a while," the forward said at his Barca unveiling last summer.

"I don't have anything bad to say as it has been an important part, not just of my career but my life, so I was grateful for the opportunity. I wish them all the best and hope they are successful in the future."

Barring an unexpected late twist, that future will now include him.

If his return to United is in line with the club's other World Cup players, who have all come back about three weeks after their final game in the tournament, he will be involved in next week's Maynooth training camp in the Republic of Ireland.

Should that happen, his first game could be against an AC Milan side managed by former boss Ruben Amorim, in Wroclaw on 15 August, depending on what his current manager, Michael Carrick, views as the wisdom of Rashford featuring against Leeds at Croke Park on 12 August with just a couple of days' training behind him.

At virtually every stage of the past year, the expectation was Rashford would not spend the 2026-27 season at Manchester United.

He scored 11 goals and made 14 assists as Barca won the La Liga title, the Spanish Super Cup and reached the Champions League quarter-finals.

When Barcelona decided not to activate the £26m clause to buy the 28-year-old, whose United contract expires in 2028, it was thought to be a negotiating tactic, aimed at taking Rashford on another loan.

But the signing of German winger Karim Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund on 23 July, following the arrival of England winger Anthony Gordon, seemed to end that possibility.

Rashford posted a farewell note to the club on social media on 30 July. A day later, Barca manager Hansi Flick was asked about the forward following a pre-season game at Birmingham.

"He is a fantastic player and a fantastic person," said Flick. "The team miss him, I will miss him, but it is life. This is what we have to accept."

That reality has created a new one.

Rashford is contracted to Manchester United until 2028. His salary of £325,000 a week makes him the club's top earner at a time when minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe is trying to stay on top of wage costs, which is, by some distance, the club's highest expenditure.

United's transfer activity has slowed since Belgium midfielder Youri Tielemans joined them for £35m on 14 July.

While uncertainty over Rashford's future is not the entire reason for this, it is a basic truth that United's search for a left-sided attacking player, or another striker, will be affected if he stays at the club because he can play in both positions.

Equally, the amount United can pay in wages will differ depending on whether Rashford's salary is part of the overall bill.

Plenty feel Rashford's fallout with Amorim over his performances in training was reflective of someone who no longer felt the joy of playing for his boyhood club.

Comparisons were made with his performances prior to his exit from United and those at Aston Villa, with England and then Barcelona.

Others think Rashford is too good to be discarded; a local lad who would benefit from an arm around the shoulder and is capable of making a significant impact in Carrick's team.

The secondary point to that is could United sign a player of similar standing for £26m, given that is the fee sources close to Rashford feel would not be exceeded given it had been agreed with Barcelona?

Rashford is 15th in United's all-time goalscorers chart with 138. He needs 17 more to equal Paul Scholes in 10th spot.

Thirty-two of those goals were scored with Carrick as a team-mate.

Carrick also coached Rashford, then managed him for three games in a 10-day spell in 2021 between Ole Gunnar Solskjaer getting sacked and Ralf Rangnick being brought in as the Norwegian's temporary replacement.

The pair are said to get on well.

Any return under Amorim would have been reminiscent of Jadon Sancho's peace deal with Erik ten Hag that got through one pre-season trip to the USA and a seven-minute Community Shield appearance against Manchester City before he moved to Chelsea on loan.

But it is possible to see Carrick and Rashford working together with a degree of permanence.

Carrick is yet to speak to the wider media since United returned to pre-season training.

An expected partially open training session in Maynooth early next week has been scrapped, so, if Rashford does return as anticipated, there will be no external cameras to catch it.

Clubs in the Premier League and overseas have inquired about Rashford and will surely continue to do so until the transfer window closes on 1 September.

Manchester United continue to insist there will be no cut-price deal or loan.

Unless something significant happens in the coming days, Rashford's return will be complete.

title: Michigan’s top election official wins Democratic primary for governor, advances to battleground race
description: Jocelyn Benson defeated Chris Swanson in Michigan's Democratic gubernatorial primary and will face either John James or Perry Johnson this fall.
fullText:
Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson on Tuesday captured the Democratic nomination for governor in the crucial Great Lakes battleground state in the race to succeed term-limited Gov. Gretchen Whitmer.

Benson defeated Genesee County Sheriff Chris Swanson in the Democratic gubernatorial primary, The Associated Press reported.

Michigan's top election official for the past eight years will now work to keep the governor's office in Democratic Party hands as Republicans aim to flip the seat.

Benson will face off in the general election against either Rep. John James or multi-millionaire businessman Perry Johnson, who are facing off for the GOP nomination.

Fox News Power Rankings: Top 2026 Governors Races

A former Wayne State University Law School dean, Benson won election as secretary of state in 2018 and re-election four years later. Benson grabbed national attention in 2020, when she defended Michigan's election systems and pushed back against President Donald Trump's unsubstantiated claims that massive voter fraud was to blame for his loss to former President Joe Biden, who narrowly carried Michigan.

Benson touts her track record in Lansing, including election security and efficiency in office, as she runs for governor. And her campaign has focused on protecting democracy, lowering costs for families, expanding affordable housing, defending reproductive rights and improving public education.

Democracy '26: Stay Up To Date With The Fox News Election Hub

The secretary of state had a large fundraising and polling advantage over Swanson heading into Michigan's primary.

Swanson grabbed national attention in the summer of 2020, when protests from coast to coast broke out over the death of George Floyd. Swanson was credited with keeping the peace as he took off his body armor to march with protesters in Flint, Michigan.

Four years later, Swanson spoke at the 2024 Democratic National Convention in Chicago as a vocal supporter of Biden and then-Vice President Kamala Harris, who replaced Biden as the party's presidential nominee after he quit the race following a disastrous debate against Trump.

title: Big money propels Dem megachurch pastor to victory in longshot Kansas Senate bid
description: Adam Hamilton won Kansas Democrats' 11-way primary to challenge Sen. Roger Marshall, who calls the megachurch pastor "too woke for Kansas."
fullText:
Kansas Democrats have made their choice in one of the most crowded primary battles in the nation and are backing a political newcomer with an eye-popping campaign war chest.

Adam Hamilton emerged victorious in an 11-way primary Tuesday night in the race to take on incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., who is running for a second term in the upper chamber.

And he has a line of attack against Hamilton already teed up.

Democrats Blink As Schumer Helps Gop Clear Key Shutdown Hurdle

"Look, this guy is a woke, big megachurch pastor," Marshall told Fox News Digital. "He's too woke for Kansas. I think all we have to do is share his own sermons … with the Kansas people, and they're gonna realize that he's too woke for Kansas."

Hamilton's campaign countered in a statement to Fox News Digital that Marshall's voting record spoke for itself.

"Roger Marshall would rather attack a church whose community is one of the largest sources of food donations in his alleged home state than talk about why he constantly votes for higher prices, why he's been hiding from Kansans for over 500 days, and why only 27 named Kansans donated to his campaign last quarter," Tyson Brody, a spokesperson for Hamilton's campaign, said.

History is on the side of Marshall, who previously served four years in the House before making the leap to the Senate in 2020. That's because Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the Senate in nearly a century. The last time was in the 1930s, when Kansans elected former Sen. George McGill. He only served one term before being ousted by a Republican.

Trump Demand Puts Vulnerable Republicans In Impossible Spot Ahead Of Midterms

Still, Marshall is not resting on his laurels as he stares down another likely funding disadvantage.

National Republicans aren't dumping resources into Kansas like they are in other states, given that Marshall is a strong incumbent and valuable campaign cash is needed in tougher contests in Texas, Maine and Ohio.

While Kansas is not on Senate Republicans' radar as a battleground state, there is big money flowing in that could make Marshall's bid for another term complicated.

Supreme Court Strikes Down Limit On Party Campaign Spending In Coordination With Candidates

Hamilton, who leads the nation's largest United Methodist church and congregation, has raised just north of $4.1 million since launching his campaign in February, according to financial filings with the Federal Election Commission.

Marshall, on the other hand, has raised just over $6.2 million during this cycle.

"Well, this is probably why my staff tells me, no matter what the polls show, they tell me that we're down by three points, and we did get outspent about four to one last time around. Regardless, we're gonna keep working hard," Marshall said.

And as precious campaign resources flow to other marquee races during this cycle, where the GOP has more vulnerable incumbents up for reelection than Democrats, Marshall isn't asking for a handout.

He wants the resources from major GOP campaign arms, like the National Republican Senatorial Committee or the GOP leadership-aligned Senate Leadership Fund, to stay put.

"I guess we're trying to not need to do that," Marshall said. "That's what our hope is, is that they won't need to do that. Leader McConnell was super helpful last time. So, you know, they're keeping tabs on this. We got to, you know, we're all one, big happy family here, so we're hoping we don't need them."

title: Bessent’s Yen gamble is a warning sign — buckle up
description: Fasten your seat belts: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has become a Big Player in the yen market. Increased volatility is right around the corner.
fullText:
Last week, U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent joined with Japan's Ministry of Finance to intervene in currency markets in an effort to boost the yen to levels that Bessent proclaimed would be more appropriate. Bessent decided that markets are not valuing the yen correctly. Apparently, a host of traders with skin in the game have it all wrong; Bessent knows better. Bessent started tongues wagging by saying in a Fox Business interview that the yen was "very undervalued" and "excess volatility" isn't healthy.

There is no question that Bessent's activity in the yen market qualifies as that of a Big Player. Recall our earlier piece in Fortune, in which we laid out the characteristics of a Big Player. Big Players are big because their words and deeds move markets. They are insensitive to profit and loss. They are also discretionary because they are not bound by any simple, understandable rules. They act on judgments that oscillate with their mood swings. So, fasten your seat belts. Forget the exchange rates thrown up by the markets. Bessent will act to move the yen to levels he deems appropriate, whatever they might happen to be.

Following the intervention of Bessent and Japan's Ministry of Finance, the yen strengthened in what may or may not turn out to be a dead cat bounce. Just why did the yen strengthen? First, there was the actual intervention, which consisted of direct purchases of the yen. Second, and more importantly, there was jawboning from U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama. Both made it clear that they wanted a stronger yen and that they were going to intervene to give the dying yen a little life. Big Players' say-so moves markets. This sort of manipulation produces volatility and perplexes markets.

As it turns out, Bessent is following an old and discredited playbook. In 1887, Ivan Vyshnegradsky replaced Nicolai Bunge as czarist Imperial Russia's finance minister. Bunge was a principled non-interventionist. He was not a Big Player. Vyshnegradsky, however, was the very archetype of a Big Player. He eagerly manipulated the ruble's exchange rate against the gold-based German mark. He was even reported to have rubbed his hands in glee once when he thought he had gotten the better of Berlin speculators. Just take a look at the accompanying figure. It shows what Big Player Vyshnegradsky's interventions accomplished.

Vyshnegradsky's interventions increased volatility. Vyshnegradsky's successor, Sergei Witte, offers the counterpoint. Rather than freelancing with discretionary interventions, Witte committed the ruble to the gold standard in 1897. For Witte, the rule-based gold standard was a symbol of Imperial Russia's standing and equality with others in the international capitalist order. The calm that followed was no accident: research on central bank interventions shows they work far better when defending a currency's rise than when trying to force it down, exactly the kind of asymmetry a rules-based system sidesteps entirely. Rules constrain; Big Players improvise. This is just what the economic theory of Big Players predicts. Contrary to Bessent's assertions, Big Player interventions in currency markets create more volatility, not less.

title: Shifting left, Democrats see universal health care, taxing the rich as 'essential,' Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
description: Liberal Democrats now make up a clear majority of their party and view universal healthcare, greater abortion access and higher taxes on the rich as essential political
fullText:
WASHINGTON, Aug 4 (Reuters) - Liberal Democrats now make up a clear majority of their party and view universal healthcare, greater abortion access and higher taxes on the rich as essential political positions, underscoring how Democrats have moved leftward in recent years, according to a ‌new Reuters/Ipsos poll.

The finding comes ahead of a Tuesday Democratic primary in which left-wing doctor Abdul El-Sayed is vying against moderate U.S. Representative ‌Haley Stevens for the party's nomination to run for a Michigan U.S. Senate seat. The seat is seen as critical for Democrats' hopes of winning a majority in that chamber in the ​November midterm elections.

The six-day poll, completed on Monday, showed the proportion of Democrats who label themselves as "liberal" has risen to 71% from 55% in 2012, while the share who see themselves as "conservative" has dwindled from 33% to 16%.

Some 76% of liberal Democrats said increasing taxes on corporations and billionaires was an "essential" policy position for anyone who considers themselves a liberal, the poll found. Another 72% said the same about expanding abortion access, while 71% said achieving government-provided healthcare for all Americans was a ‌necessary goal for any liberal.

Insurgent left-wing candidates ⁠this year have racked up a string of primary victories over more centrist Democrats, many of whom were backed by the party establishment. They have gone beyond New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani's election last year in a deeply liberal city to ⁠vie for office in more politically divided states.

The Michigan primary is the latest example of that trend: Stevens is backed by Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and many top state Democrats, while El-Sayed was endorsed by liberal U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont.

Like Sanders, El-Sayed supports Medicare for All, a plan to provide public health insurance to ​all Americans ​that has become a rallying call for the insurgent left. Stevens supports strengthening subsidies ​for private health insurance.

In neighboring Wisconsin, another political swing state, ‌democratic socialist Francesca Hong appears poised to win the Democratic gubernatorial nomination despite efforts by party leaders to elevate a more moderate candidate.

The winner in Michigan will face the task of reuniting Democratic voters after a bitter primary campaign that was often dominated by the candidates' differences on Israel.

Stevens supports continued military funding for Israel and has benefited from tens of millions of dollars spent by the American Israel Public Affairs Committee backing her campaign. El-Sayed has been sharply critical of Israel, which he accuses of committing genocide in Gaza, and called for a halt to all aid.

Only 16% of Democrats support military and ‌economic support for Israel, while 57% oppose it, according to the Reuters/Ipsos poll. Among liberal ​Democrats, more than 80% said reducing or eliminating that support was either important or essential ​for any liberal; only 18% said it was not important.

Some 89% of ​Republicans responding to the poll described themselves as conservative, a more modest shift from the 82% who labeled themselves that ‌way in the 2012 poll. Despite their near-unanimity around how to ​describe themselves, conservative Republicans were less unified ​in identifying policy goals as "essential."

Some 56% said allowing fewer immigrants into the country was an essential view for conservatives, a goal that has been central to President Donald Trump's rise to power and years in office. Similarly, only 50% of conservative Republicans said reducing the size of the ​federal government was essential to being conservative -- a goal ‌long pursued by conservative officeholders.

The poll, conducted online and nationwide, gathered responses from 4,505 U.S. adults and had a margin of error ​of 2 percentage points for all respondents and 3 points for liberal Democrats and for conservative Republicans.

title: Why Trump is downplaying reports Russia and China are helping Iran
description: Trump says he'll ask Putin directly about satellite imagery allegations as experts warn Russia and China are quietly aiding Iran against U.S. forces.
fullText:
President Donald Trump cast doubt in recent days on allegations that Russia is helping Iran target U.S. forces, even as members of his own administration acknowledge Moscow and Beijing are supporting Tehran in other ways.

Trump dismissed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's claim that Russia supplied Iran with satellite imagery of U.S. military installations in the Gulf, saying any assistance would have been "very unimpactful" given the damage inflicted on Iran's military.

"We'll find out if that's true. I'll ask Putin. We'll find out," Trump told reporters at the end of July.

Waltz Warns Of Chinese, Russian-fueled 'National Security Threat' Looming Close To Us Shores

"I don't think they've been doing it, certainly not at a high level," Trump added. "And if they have, it has been very unimpactful."

Trump pointed to the damage Iran's military has suffered during the war. Russian help, he argued, has failed to stop the United States from destroying much of Tehran's conventional forces.

Trump's comments came as his administration confronted separate reports that Russia and China are helping Iran in different ways — allegations that, if borne out, would suggest America's two chief geopolitical rivals are quietly supporting a nation at war with the U.S. Members of his own administration have acknowledged broader help from Moscow and Beijing.

China's Iran Ties Complicate Trump-xi Summit As Tensions Test Us Leverage

War Secretary Pete Hegseth has said Russia and China are "enabling some of the things Iran is doing," but a White House official told Fox News Digital that any foreign assistance has failed to improve Tehran's ability to attack Americans.

Trump's comments came in response to two recent reports: Zelenskyy's allegation that Russia provided satellite intelligence to Iran and a Reuters report that China could send hundreds of shoulder-fired air-defense missiles to Tehran through Pakistan, which China has denied.

Fresh satellite imagery could help Iran locate high-value assets and refine strike coordinates, then show whether an attack hit its intended target.

"As the President stated, nothing that any outside actor is doing to help Iran is in any way increasing their ability to target Americans," the official told Fox News Digital, responding to questions about Zelenskyy's claim that Russia gave Iran satellite imagery of U.S. military installations in the Gulf.

Zelenskyy laid out Ukraine's evidence Saturday, saying Russian satellites had surveyed Gulf countries and U.S. military installations beginning in early July before the imagery later appeared in Iran.

"These images subsequently appear in Iran," Zelenskyy wrote on X.

Ukraine found what Zelenskyy described as a "clear correlation" between the Russian observations and subsequent Iranian attacks. According to Zelenskyy, Moscow collected imagery before strikes to aid targeting and returned afterward to assess the damage.

Zelenskyy said Russian satellites focused on four air bases over two days — two in Bahrain and one each in Jordan and Kuwait — and said Ukrainian intelligence had shared the information with foreign partners.

Ukrainian Ambassador to the U.S. Olga Stefanishyna said at a July 30 reporter roundtable that the allegation did not arise during Zelenskyy's White House meeting with Trump because the agenda was crowded. She said Ukraine had provided the information "through other channels."

A Ukrainian official told Fox News Digital that Kyiv wants to avoid "opening a second front" with Iran.

Hegseth acknowledged Russian and Chinese support for Iran during a Senate hearing in July.

There was "definitely adversary alignment," Hegseth said. Russia and China were "at different levels, enabling some of the things Iran is doing."

The U.S. has ways to deter that support, he added, though some of those measures should remain classified. Hegseth said earlier in the war that the administration knew "exactly" what Moscow and Beijing were doing and was addressing their actions where needed.

Russia has denied supplying Iran with intelligence on American military targets. Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said the locations of U.S. bases were publicly available. The Kremlin also dismissed earlier reporting about Russian intelligence support for Iran as false.

Trump also questioned reports that Iran could soon receive hundreds of Chinese-made shoulder-fired air-defense systems through Pakistan, saying Chinese President Xi Jinping had assured him Beijing would stay out of the conflict.

"That was surprising. I mean, things like that happen, but that would be surprising. He told me very strongly he wouldn't partake, but he knows I'd be quite disappointed. He's coming here, I think, on September 24," the president told reporters Wednesday.

Matthew Kroenig, a former Pentagon and intelligence official, called the reports "highly plausible," pointing to growing cooperation among Russia, China and Iran.

"From Russia and China's point of view, if they can complicate the U.S. war in the Middle East and raise the cost to Washington, that's a good thing for them," Kroenig told Fox News Digital.

Kroenig said Trump may be warning Moscow and Beijing privately instead of confronting them before television cameras.

"That might be the most generous interpretation, that it's his way of warning China and Russia to knock it off," he said.

Trump's comments would carry more risk if the president were relying on assurances from Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, Kroenig said. He urged the administration to make clear that either country would face a cost for helping Tehran.

"I think there would be a risk to just discounting this altogether," Kroenig said.

Anna Borshchevskaya, a senior fellow at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, said Moscow has spent years building closer military ties with Tehran.

"If this proves accurate, Russia has found a way to help Iran without direct military engagement, and that's why this is significant," Borshchevskaya told Fox News Digital.

Iran began supplying Russia with Shahed attack drones in 2022, giving Moscow a cheap weapon it could launch in waves against Ukrainian cities and power infrastructure.

Russia later began producing its own versions with Iranian support and improved the design, making the drones a mainstay of its attacks. Tehran's earlier support now hangs over Zelenskyy's claim that Moscow is helping Iran target American forces.

Satellite imagery would give Moscow another way to aid Tehran while avoiding a direct clash with American forces.

"It's hard to think how the provision of intelligence is insignificant," Borshchevskaya said.

She said Trump may be trying to keep his public exchanges with Moscow calm as U.S. officials send firmer messages in private.

Russia views the wars in Ukraine and Iran as connected parts of its campaign against American influence, Borshchevskaya said. U.S. officials tend to handle each conflict through a separate policy process.

"The challenge for us is that we often separate theaters, but Russia does not," she said. "Russia looks at all of these conflicts in a much more interconnected way."

Borshchevskaya said Russia has chosen forms of aid that can strengthen Iran without committing Russian troops or entering a direct fight with Washington.

"Russia is being restrained here," she said. "They're playing a much more nuanced game."

Trump also voiced surprise Wednesday at a report that Iran could soon receive hundreds of Chinese-made, shoulder-fired air-defense systems through Pakistan.

Xi had given Trump a firm assurance that China would stay out of the war, according to the president.

"He told me very strongly he wouldn't partake, but he knows I'd be quite disappointed," Trump said.

China called the report "groundless." Pakistan rejected the claim that it would help route the weapons to Iran, calling the allegation "baseless and devoid of truth."

Kroenig said Beijing has supplied Russia with economic and industrial support during the war in Ukraine. China has stopped short of openly sending lethal weapons, a limit he had expected Beijing to observe in the Iran war.

Advanced air defenses would require approval from the Chinese government, he said. Russian satellite intelligence would also come from state-controlled capabilities.

"There are no mom-and-pop shops in St. Petersburg selling this data," Kroenig said.

title: Taiwan launches major war games to test command flexibility
description: Taiwan began major military drills on Wednesday to test commanders' ability to fight on the fly when enemy movements defy expectations, while temporarily
fullText:
TAIPEI, Aug 5 (Reuters) - Taiwan began major military drills on Wednesday to test commanders' ability to fight on the fly when enemy movements defy expectations, while temporarily limiting internet access for the first time, senior ‌Taiwan officials said.

The 10-day annual Han Kuang exercise began early in the morning after an underground command centre in ‌Taipei issued the drill order, triggering combat-readiness moves that will include fighter jet dispersals and emergency naval deployments, two senior Taiwan officials briefed on the matter told Reuters.

Taiwan ​will also incorporate for the first time a so-called "backbrief" approach modelled on U.S. military practice, in which junior officers receiving orders restate mission details to commanders — a move aimed at improving coordination, the officials added, requesting anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter.

The move, one of the officials said, is to "ensure commanders and subordinates are in sync on operational intent."

The drill will also focus on a key wartime concern: ‌that China, which claims Taiwan as its ⁠own despite the island's objections, would try to paralyse command centres, ports, logistics and defence industry sites early in an attack.

China's defence ministry did not respond to a request for comment. China has never renounced ⁠the use of force to bring Taiwan under its control.

Held annually since 1984, the drills will include for the first time the deliberate slowing of mobile internet speeds to test how civilians would communicate if bandwidth became scarce.

The military will simulate the wartime relocation of a major arsenal, ​mobilise civilian ​factories and run escort drills off Taiwan's Pacific coast, as concern grows ​that Beijing may be rehearsing how to sever the ‌island's Pacific supply lines from allies as Chinese military pressure intensifies.

"These are all part of a series of toughening exercises — this is no longer a laboratory-like exercise in a vacuum," said a third senior official, speaking on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the operation.

"You are entering a real field environment, facing real bottom-line conditions. We hope the final phase of training reaches that state," the defence official said.

That is part of Taiwan's ongoing effort to make its exercises more realistic, following past criticism that some drills ‌were too highly staged.

The effort has included resilience drills testing how ​local officials would keep the government running during cascading crises, from earthquakes to a ​Chinese invasion.

"If the situation does not match the original ​enemy scenario, what should he do? How should he reassess, readjust, and quickly issue orders?" the defence ‌official said, referring to field commanders who will be tested ​with "unexpected scenarios" during the drills, ​which end on August 14.

The drills will also mobilise more than 20,000 reservists.

On the sports field of a Taipei high school on Wednesday, dozens of reservists gathered to practise using mortars and taking up rifle positions.

The military will also introduce an "embedded ​reporter" mechanism to assess wartime frontline news ‌releases and efforts to counter enemy disinformation, the officials said.

"The emphasis will be on how our entire population, the ​Republic of China as a whole — especially our citizens — should face war," the defence official said, using Taiwan's official ​name.

title: Devastated mother blames soft-on-crime policies after career criminal is charged in son’s death
description: Jacob Freytes' family pushes for mandatory life sentences for child killers after the 12-year-old was fatally struck by a stray bullet in the Bronx.
fullText:
The family of a 12-year-old boy killed by a stray bullet in the Bronx is demanding change after a suspect with a lengthy arrest record was charged with his murder.

After the death of Jacob Freytes, the son of a retired NYPD detective sergeant, his mother and sister are pushing for "Jacob's Law," which they say would require life sentences for people convicted of recklessly taking a child's life.

"I gave him a kiss, and I walked out, and we always do a little dolphin kiss. And I walked out and went to work," Migdalia Martinez, Freytes' mother, told "Fox & Friends" Tuesday.

2 Detained After Shooting In New York Leaves 15-Year-old Killed, Two Others Wounded: Police

"Around five o'clock, they called me and said that he had gotten shot. And all I could do was try to think of different ways to get here faster," she added. "When I got there, I just seen my boy gone."

Freytes, who was riding his bike to a nearby bodega to buy a ball, was shot and killed after a suspect opened fire during an alleged street dispute. Two other adults were also wounded in the shooting.

Police said William Ferrer, 45, was arrested and faces multiple charges, including second-degree murder. He has pleaded not guilty. Ferrer has an arrest record dating back more than 25 years, including prior charges for drunk driving, drug possession, menacing and criminal contempt, according to the New York Post.

New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch addressed Ferrer's arrest on X, writing, "Jacob was an innocent bystander on his bike when he was taken from his family yesterday in an act of senseless gun violence.

House Democrat Blasted After Early Release Law Freed Inmates Later Charged With Murder

"No arrest can ever ease the pain of this unimaginable loss, but the NYPD will continue to do everything in our power to seek justice for Jacob."

The family is calling for a proposed "Jacob's Law" that they say would require life sentences for people convicted of recklessly taking a child's life. The family also criticized New York's crime policies, including cash bail reforms for misdemeanors and the end of stop-and-frisk.

"It's just so much that they allow that, at this point, it's just safer more for the criminals than it is for hardworking people," Martinez said.

Freytes' sister, Angelica Coriano, said the family welcomed the charges but remained uneasy about whether the suspect would receive enough prison time if convicted.

Louisiana Bill Expands First-degree Murder Charges And Death Penalty Eligibility After Mall Shooting

"'Jacob's Law' will allow for there to be no in-between whether somebody goes to jail or not for taking a child's life recklessly. It'll allow for criminals to go straight to jail or prison instead of the family having to go to court continuously hoping and wondering if they're [going to] get the justice that they deserve for the child that they lost," Coriano said.

"And we went to court and found out all the charges that he'd be receiving, which is great, but we still have to sit with the worry whether he'll face all the time that is necessary enough to keep him where he needs to be. And that type of uncertainty is very uncomfortable for us as a family, knowing that we'll never see our child again."

Martinez remembered her son as a "funny, quirky kid" who loved his friends, family and playing video games.

"There wasn't an old woman he didn't help with bags or cross the street," she said. "There wasn't a person that if he caught your eye, he'd make sure to tell you hi."

title: Behind closed doors, Trump, White House aides hope Rep. Max Miller exits race
description: Some White House officials hope embattled GOP Rep. Max Miller exits his congressional race immediately, and President Trump has expressed a similar sentiment, multiple sources say.
fullText:
Washington — Some White House officials hope embattled GOP Rep. Max Miller exits the congressional race in Ohio immediately, and President Trump has expressed a similar sentiment behind closed doors, multiple U.S. officials familiar with the matter tell CBS News.

Mr. Trump called Miller on Monday and raised concerns about his reelection bid following allegations that Miller assaulted his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, and their 2-year-old daughter, two sources directly familiar with the call confirmed to CBS News. But Miller, who has adamantly denied the allegations, told the president he has no plans to leave the race, according to one of the sources.

Miller, the GOP nominee, has until 4 p.m. Wednesday to withdraw his candidacy and give Republicans a chance to replace him on the ballot in November. Semafor first reported that the president and some White House aides said privately that they wanted Miller out of the race.

On Tuesday morning, Miller said he would file the paperwork to launch a congressional ethics investigation into himself in an effort to clear his name.

"In light of all the renewed interest in my family affairs I am going to file my own paperwork for an ethics investigation into myself to clear my name from these horrific attacks on myself and family," Miller wrote on X. "I have absolutely nothing to hide. We will be providing the committee all necessary documents needed for a detail[ed] examination. The accusations continue to change, but my facts stay the same. I am looking forward to my colleagues reading everything for themselves."

On Monday, the president said he thought Miller was a "very good person" and said he would let the families involved resolve the situation.

"Well, it's a very sad thing," the president told reporters in the Oval Office Monday. "I know Max, he's a good person, I mean, I always thought he was a very good person. And I'm going to let the families figure that out. Those families, I know they're working on it. It's a very sad thing. Especially when you know somebody so well to be going through that. But it's accusations. And I'm going to let them figure that out."

In an earlier statement to CBS News on Monday, Miller said: "If I dropped out of this race, it would mean we as a nation have fallen so far from our American values. I will not validate false claims by removing myself just to please the court of public opinion. I am innocent of all of the allegations that have been attributed to me. I have done well representing my constituents' interests. Why would I drop out?"

Emily Moreno, Miller's ex-wife, is the daughter of Ohio GOP Sen. Bernie Moreno. The senator said in a statement on Sunday that Miller "should not serve in the House of Representatives" and "needs serious psychological help."

description: When in the course of human events it becomes necessary to throw off the shackles of laziness and write the column you’ve been thinking about for months, you gotta do it. My daughter is 11 and a K-Pop fiend and I was at H-Mart Sunday when one of her favorite songs was playing. I knew […]
fullText:
When in the course of human events it becomes necessary to throw off the shackles of laziness and write the column you've been thinking about for months, you gotta do it. My daughter is 11 and a K-Pop fiend and I was at H-Mart Sunday when one of her favorite songs was playing. I knew every word and the cashier loved it. On my way to the car, I realized that my work for the day was only beginning, as this column needed to escape my fingers. I took Sunday's lineup who warrant mentioning and came up with the appropriate K-Pop song my daughter adores for each of 'em. As she only listens to girl groups, this will consist solely of girl groups. This list is correct and final and beings now.

Aespa is a relatively new addition to my daughter's rotation, which largely revolves around Illit (pronounced "eyelet") to whom we will get shortly. In fact, this song is the most recent addition to her rotation. Because of/despite being a certain age I generally do not comment on the looks of K-Pop idols, but when L showed me the video I said, "even for K-Pop, these are extraordinary good looking people," and she agreed. That's not why it's Eric Sogard tho. It's Eric Sogard because it's about making lemonades out of lemons, or so I imagine, and when Eric Sogard is batting leadoff for your playoff-eligible team in 2026 that's exactly what you're doing (complimentary):

This is the song I heard in H-Mart, by L's favorite group, about which she is sort of a hipster but has a point. They have bangers. Their name is an echo of the phrase "I'll do it" with the "do" take out, hence "eyelet." This is their most popular song, and it's about magnetism, like Ceddy to the ball in the outfield. It just works. Both the analogy and the song.

The bounces and clutch hits it took for Wilyer Abreu to become who is he to Red Sox Nation is don't happen for 99 out of the other 100 guys trying to hack it in MLB. If anyone on this team is "iconic by mistake," it's him, so he gets this L fever-dream banger from American K-Pop group Katseye, Korea's Le Sserafim (an anagram of "I'm fearless") and Illit. And it is a banger, full-stop. He earned it, and they had to come together like a three-headed Voltron to match his status. Everyone wins.

There were harder song choices to match to players than this, but as a guy who likes hitting homers and other players in the face, Willson gets "Bang Bang." Sometimes it do be that simple:

Who wouldn't be jealous of a fully guaranteed $90 million contract?

At the time of this typing, the Brewers are tied with the Dodgers for the best record in baseball. Until the last coupla months, coming to Boston in the offseason must have felt like a punishment. Now that he's back in the playoff hunt — thanks not leastwise because of his own work — he's gotta feel like the luckiest guy in Boston. Certainly luckier than Curtis Mead. Too soon?

Literally because his last name sounds Italian. That's it.

title: Adley Rutschman ‘trying to fit in’ with Red Sox while working his way back from injury
description: “Just from playing here, the city loves baseball. It always has a great atmosphere and I’m excited to play in it."
fullText:
BOSTON (AP) — Adley Rutschman was still adjusting less than 24 hours after being traded for the first time in his career.

Being in playoff contention may make for a smoother transition once the three-time All-Star catcher is ready to take the field for the Red Sox after spending his first four-plus seasons with the Baltimore Orioles.

"Just from playing here, the city loves baseball. It always has a great atmosphere and I'm excited to play in it," Rutschman said Tuesday at Fenway Park before the Red Sox hosted the Chicago White Sox. "They're playing the game the right way and doing things right. It was cool to watch from a distance. Now being here, like I said — just trying to fit in and help out any way I can."

Rutschman joined his new club on the injured list with left wrist inflammation. He and Boston interim manager Chad Tracy said Rutschman would meet with the team's medical staff to determine what's next in his rehabilitation and how soon he could be back behind the plate.

Tracy said Rutschman is already swinging a bat and the Red Sox were hopeful to add him to their lineup soon. Boston also wasn't about to rush the recovery of a player that cost it a handful of top prospects in a deal pulled off shortly before Monday's trade deadline.

"It's been feeling good. I've got to get with the medical staff here and kind of just see what the next steps are moving forward," said Rutschman, who's been on the IL since July 20. "I don't exactly know just what kind of timeline and how all that goes."

Rutschman moved from the Orioles, who were 12 games back in the AL East and on the fringes of the wild-card race entering Tuesday night, to the Red Sox, who were 5 1/2 games out of the division lead and in position for a wild card after winning 23 of their last 26 games.

The Orioles stopped Boston's franchise record-tying winning streak at 15 games last month, but reaching the playoffs appeared less likely for Baltimore without Rutschman, the top overall pick in the 2019 draft.

"I played my entire career there and there's been a lot of unbelievable memories. Just made a lot of great friends for life," Rutschman said. "It's tough goodbyes. But we're on to the next thing. And excited to be here and playing. It's all part of the game."

Rutschman said part of his down time will include getting to know Boston's pitchers, although there was already some familiarity.

"I've seen a lot of these guys pitch and faced them," Rutschman said. "I kind of understand how they attack guys but I'm definitely going to have some more in-depth conversations, just make sure that we're on the same page and it flows smoothly when we get out there."

Whenever that is, Boston will be glad to have him.

"I think it's a strong statement to the group with a player like that," Tracy said. "We went out and got a huge addition to our lineup and behind the plate. So it means a lot. We'll work through getting him healthy and getting him out there. But his history speaks for itself and who he is as a catcher and as an offensive player. So it's a big add for us."

title: Lakers Proposed to Trade Bronny James to 76ers in New Deal for 41% 3-Pt Sniper
description: With the Los Angeles Lakers’ current roster count exceeding the NBA-mandated limit, we know another move is on the way. The Lakers have had no shortage of new names this offseason. fullText:
With the Los Angeles Lakersâ current roster count exceeding the NBA-mandated limit, we know another move is on the way.

The Lakers have had no shortage of new names this offseason. The floodgates bursted open after LeBron James, currently the leagueâs oldest player and the all time leading scorer, informed the Lakers he wasnât going to return for a ninth season with the franchise. From there, L.A. pivoted as the Luka Doncic era was officially underway.Â

Jamesâ exit was naturally going to stir up heavy speculation about his sonâs future. Bronny James, whose contract for the 2026-26 season was guaranteed the day before his fatherâs decision to leave the Lakers, is now being linked to the Philadelphia 76ersâ after the elder Jamesâ decision to sign with the franchise.Â

GettyLAS VEGAS, NEVADA – OCTOBER 15: LeBron James (L) #23 and Bronny James #9 of the Los Angeles Lakers warm up before a preseason game against the Golden State Warriors at T-Mobile Arena at T-Mobile Arena on October 15, 2024 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images)

So far, there is no evidence that the Lakers are actively seeking trade partners for the younger James nor that the Sixers are attempting to get the two Jameses together again. But if the Lakers can return some nice assets in exchange for the younger James, a trade may be on the table.

In a hypothetical scenario, the Lakers dial up the Sixers and Detroit Pistons to execute a deal that would ship Bronny to the City of Brotherly Love and a sharpshooting wing to L.A.Â

Lakers receive: Duncan Robinson and two second round picks (via DET)

Pistons receive: Jaden Hardy, Dalton Knecht and a 2031 second round pick (via LAL)

This unique framework would be a nice win for the Lakers. Acquiring Robinson, a career 40 percent 3-point shooter, next to Doncic, ever the playmaking savant, is the exact formula that Doncic-led teams thrive on.Â

For Philadelphia, it would be as simple as getting both Jameses together again. If it happens, it will be because of LeBronâs request.

For Detroit, moving Robinsonâs $16 million salary for a quality role player in Hardy and a young sharpshooter in Knecht is strong value. Add to that a second round pick.Â

Itâs not like the Lakers are stockpiled with 3-point marksmen. As currently constructed, perhaps L.A.âs only dependable role-playing perimeter shooter may be Quentin Grimes, who was added as a part of the teamâs flurry of free agent signings.

Robinson, 32, only provides one thing, and itâs the most important thing going: elite 3-point shooting. As a starter for the Pistons last season, Robinson, who has a pair of NBA Finals appearances under his belt, averaged roughly 12 points per game. Roughly nine of the 12 came from long-distance.Â

For the Lakers, Robinson could be exactly the kind of player the team can plug into the lineup down the stretch to hit some timely 3-pointers.Â

While Lakers fans always struggle with the idea that elite shooters somehow get worse playing for L.A., Robinson has gone through multiple playoff runs. He was a key figure for two Miami Heat teams that somehow blitzed through the Eastern Conference to reach the Finals.

title: Packers’ Micah Parsons eyeing Week 6 vs. Cowboys for return from ACL tear
description: Packers star Micah Parsons is hoping to be back from his ACL tear by Week 6 against his old team, the Cowboys.
fullText:
Packers' Micah Parsons eyeing Week 6 vs. Cowboys for return from ACL tear appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The Green Bay Packers are hoping to contend for an NFC Championship again this season, as they have one of the best rosters in the NFC coming into the season. However, they are still working on getting all of their stars healthy from an injury-riddled 2025 season before Week 1.

Unfortunately, it looks like Micah Parsons' knee injury is going to linger into the season. The star pass rusher tore his ACL in a game against the Denver Broncos late in the season and missed the remainder of the year. He has spent the entire offseason rehabbing, but is currently on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list during training camp and is expected to be sidelined for Week 1 and beyond.

Now, Parsons has revealed a potential target date for his return. The Packers play against his old team, the Dallas Cowboys, in Week 6 on Oct. 18, and Parsons says it is a possibility he will be back for that game, per Ryan Wood of USA Today.

"Is it possible? Yes, so I wouldn't say it's not possible," Parsons said. "At the same time, in the next 10, 12 weeks from now, we've got to make it possible by putting the work in."

It's not ideal that the Packers will have to play any games without Parsons on the field, but thankfully it sounds like he should be back by midseason. The former Penn State star transformed the Packers' defense last season after Green Bay acquired him in a trade with the Cowboys. If they want to make a push for a Super Bowl this season, they need him back at 100%.

Thankfully for the Packers, star tight end Tucker Kraft is already back on the field after recovering from his torn ACL. Kraft was seen biking out to training camp last week and has been taken off of the PUP list. Kraft suffered his injury earlier last season, so it's a good sign to see him already back on the field.

If the Packers want to make a run this year, they will need both Parsons and Kraft to be back at their best.

title: Montreal’s Arber Xhekaj Was Targeted By A Canadian-Based Rival
description: Following their successful 2025-26 season that saw them advance to the Eastern Conference Final, the Montreal Canadiens and general manager Kent Hughes re-signed both Ivan Demidov and Jakub Dobes to multi-year contracts.The good news for the Canadiens is that they appear set up to be a force in the Atlantic Division for a long time […] The post Montreal’s Arber Xhekaj Was Targeted By A Canadian-Based Rival appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Following their successful 2025-26 season that saw them advance to the Eastern Conference Final, the Montreal Canadiens and general manager Kent Hughes re-signed both Ivan Demidov and Jakub Dobes to multi-year contracts.

The good news for the Canadiens is that they appear set up to be a force in the Atlantic Division for a long time with so many of their core pieces locked up for the foreseeable future under contract. However, one player that still is in need of a few deal before next season is hard-nosed defenseman Arber Xhekaj.

Currently, he's a restricted free agent following the expiration of his most recent contract that carried a salary cap hit of $1.3 million.

According to Herb Zurkowsky of The Montreal Gazette, the Calgary Flames showed interest in Xhekaj at last season's NHL Trade Deadline.

"Another source revealed Calgary's interest in Xhekaj last season at the trade deadline," he wrote.

According to NHL Insider David Pagnotta, there isn't much to report in terms of movement on a new deal between the Canadiens and Xhekaj.

"At the time we're doing this right now, the update is status quo conversationally between the Habs and Xekaj," he said. "They're not the only one to want to have that sandpaper in the lineup, there are other teams that have expressed over the last few weeks interest in trading for Arber Xhekaj, but the Canadiens have valued him for some time and they haven't pulled the trigger. A, they haven't found a deal they want because B, they want to keep the player. You've gotta convince them to make it happen."

Pagnotta then revealed that one of the clubs that showed interest in Xhekaj was the Philadelphia Flyers, a club that always welcomes grit and sandpaper in their lineup.

"The very quick update with respect to Xhekaj and the Canadiens, despite interest from other teams – I mean, Philadelphia is one, and they've had interest in him during the last couple of years and is still the case now – but nothing done on that front yet," he said. "And contractually, status quo. They'll go back and forth to try and bridge whatever gap there is; both sides being very quiet on that side."

Pagnotta's words of there not being any rush to get a deal done for Xhekaj were recently confirmed by his agent Brian Bartlett, who noted that there is still plenty of time between now and the start of next season.

"We have a long time until the season starts," Bartlett said. "We have to try and figure out where he fits into the structure of the team. Montreal has some decisions to make. We have some decisions to make. There's no panic."

"I think he's a really good player," he continued. "Good teams like good players. The communication has been positive with the management group. I don't have any indication to think that things are going to go off the rail."

title: Atlanta Braves Release Andrew McCutchen From Minor League Contract
description: The Braves released McCutchen, who did not appear with the big league team after being signed to a minor-league contract in early July.
fullText:
The Braves released the veteran outfielder after a month in their organization.

The Atlanta Braves announced they have released outfielder Andrew McCutchen from his minor league contract.

McCutchen had signed a minor league deal with the team last month and had been playing with Triple-A Gwinnett, with hopes of working his way back up to the major leagues.

The transaction was McCutchen exercising an opt-out clause in his contract with Atlanta, per Stephen J. Nesbitt of The Athletic. He most likely wants a better path to the big leagues instead of cracking his way into the Braves' outfield.

With the recent addition of right-handed outfielder Lane Thomas to the Braves' roster, whom they acquired from the Kansas City Royals at the trade deadline, Atlanta essentially fulfilled their need for a right-handed bat at the position, while not opting to select McCutchen. He did not play a game for the Braves' big league team this season.

McCutchen, now 39, signed his minor league contract with the Braves on July 2, a little over a month after he had been released by the Texas Rangers in late May. He had played in parts of 37 games with the Rangers this season, posting a .192 batting average in 73 at-bats.

In what turned out to be a very short stint with Triple-A Gwinnett, McCutchen had himself a solid stretch in just 30 at-bats. In nine games, he hit .333 at the plate and recorded 10 hits.

The former NL MVP with the Pittsburgh Pirates had broken camp with the Rangers and made their Opening Day roster. Now well beyond his prime, his bat has primarily been utilized as a platoon against left-handed pitching, his strong suit at the plate.

McCutchen had made his return to Pittsburgh in 2023 after playing for four separate teams in between his initial stint with the team, and performed at a very productive level. From 2023-2025, even in the later years of his career, he impressed as a league-average bat and a lefty specialist.

Atlanta's release of McCutchen was not the only release of a veteran in their organization. Left-handed pitcher Austin Gomber and outfielder Ben Gamel were also released from their Triple-A affiliate.

McCutchen still may factor into the mix of a team's outfield, though doing so for a contender may be unlikely for the right-handed bat now in the back half of his career. After the deadline, the Braves now add Thomas to an outfield that consists of Ronald Acuña Jr, Michael Harris and Mike Yastrzemski.

title: Jesse Minter’s clear standard is accelerating the Ravens' transition
description: Mike Mickens credits Jesse Minter with creating a clear standard that keeps Baltimore’s defensive coaches and players aligned.
fullText:
The Baltimore Ravens assembled their new defensive staff from different levels of football and several coaching backgrounds. Jesse Minter's first challenge was ensuring all of those voices delivered one message. Mike Mickens believes the new head coach has accomplished that through a clearly defined standard.

"He has us on the same page, and he has a clear message," Mickens said on The Ravens Lounge. "We want to be the best in everything that we do."

Mickens arrived from Notre Dame to become Baltimore's defensive pass game coordinator and secondary coach. Anthony Weaver returned as defensive coordinator, while other assistants carried experience from different NFL and college systems. Those perspectives can strengthen a staff, but they can also create confusion if position coaches use conflicting terminology or teach different responses to the same situation. Minter's leadership is intended to remove that gray area. Players should hear the same philosophy regardless of which coach leads the meeting or corrects a practice rep.

The approach is particularly important in the secondary. Defensive backs must communicate coverage checks, route distribution and motions within seconds. A hesitation by one player can turn a routine adjustment into an explosive completion. Mickens said the staff has clearly explained its processes and expectations from the top down. That consistency allows assistants to focus on technique without creating questions about the defense's larger objective.

Baltimore is also working through a significant transition after an 8-9 season led to the departure of longtime coach John Harbaugh. Players are learning Minter's system while adjusting to new teachers and practice expectations. A complicated defensive playbook becomes manageable when the coaching points remain consistent. Minter's task is to make sure the same language connects the meeting room, practice field, and game-day headset.

The Ravens will ultimately judge the system by points allowed, takeaways and victories. Before those results arrive, Minter is establishing the shared understanding required to produce them.

According to Mickens, every defensive coach already knows the standard he is expected to reinforce.

title: Blue Jays pitcher suddenly leaves game while warming up

fullText:
Trey Yesavage's latest start ended earlier than expected.

Reliever Chad Dallas replaced Yesavage in the bottom of the third inning at Daikin Park in Houston.

The cause of the injury is unclear. Whatever ailed him, it did not appear to affect Yesavage's right arm. He tapped his left (landing) foot a couple times before he was visited by Schneider and the trainer. He stepped somewhat gingerly on the foot as they walked off.

The Blue Jays have not announced why Yesavage left the game.

After winning the American League pennant a year ago, the Blue Jays got off to a 53-60 start 2026, all but mathematically eliminating them from contention. They traded pitcher Kevin Gausman to the Chicago Cubs ahead of the trade deadline on Monday, Aug. 3.

Toronto also acquired pitcher Jose Soriano from the Los Angeles Angels to replace Gausman. Now they might need to find a substitute for Yesavage, who has been their second-best starter behind Dylan Cease.

title: Brewers send pitcher Brandon Sproat to Triple-A after acquiring Dustin May
description: With the Milwaukee Brewers’ trade-deadline acquisition of veteran starter Dustin May, rookie right-hander Brandon Sproat became the odd man out of the rotation.  Sproat, who appeared in 21 games for Milwaukee, including 19 starts, was optioned Tuesday to Triple-A Nashville one day after another inconsistent start.  May, acquired from the Cardinals on Monday along with reliever JoJo Romero, is scheduled to start Thursday for Milwaukee in the series finale against Pittsburgh.
fullText:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — With the Milwaukee Brewers' trade-deadline acquisition of veteran starter Dustin May, rookie right-hander Brandon Sproat became the odd man out of the rotation.

Sproat, who appeared in 21 games for Milwaukee, including 19 starts, was optioned Tuesday to Triple-A Nashville one day after another inconsistent start.

May, acquired from the Cardinals on Monday along with reliever JoJo Romero, is scheduled to start Thursday for Milwaukee in the series finale against Pittsburgh. Left-hander Kyle Harrison, on the injured list since July 9, also is scheduled to return and start Wednesday.

The 25-year-old Sproat, acquired from the Mets in the offseason trade for Freddy Peralta, is 3-7 with a 5.27 ERA for Milwaukee. He has not won in five starts since his last victory on June 30.

"I think you look at it at face value. It wasn't a foregone conclusion," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said before Tuesday's game. "It's really about what's best for the player and what's best for the team."

Sproat took the loss Monday in a 4-3 defeat in the series opener against the Pirates, allowing four runs on five hits in three-plus innings. He was removed after throwing consecutive wild pitches following a leadoff single in the fourth.

Sproat has struck out 100 in 95 2/3 innings with the Brewers. But he walked 48, hit nine batters and threw nine wild pitches.

"The free bases, the wild pitches, the walks, hit by pitches, has got to stop," Murphy said. "You can't pitch in the big leagues like that."

May was 5-7 with a 4.38 ERA in 21 starts with St. Louis, including 0-1 with a 4.62 ERA in six July starts.

The Brewers also optioned reliever Garrett Stallings to Nashville on Tuesday. In addition to getting Romero, Milwaukee also acquired reliever Antonio Senzatela from Colorado on Monday.

title: Terry McLaurin Issues Clear Message Amid Commanders’ WR Concerns
description: Washington Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin is trying to be a calming influence as the team deals with major questions at his position. The post Terry McLaurin Issues Clear Message Amid Commanders’ WR Concerns appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Washington Commanders have several questions at wide receiver with the second week of training camp now in full swing, but Terry McLaurin assured the team and its fans that they need not worry about the position group — at least not at the very top.

McLaurin held out for a new contract last offseason following a Pro Bowl and second-team All-Pro campaign. He ultimately landed a three-year contract worth $97 million, but stumbled in 2025 due to the first meaningful injury concerns of his career (quad strain and ankle sprain).

For the first time since his rookie year in 2019, McLaurin failed to eclipse 1,000 receiving yards. Quarterback Jayden Daniels also battled injuries all season long and played in just seven contests. The result was a 5-12 record, the exact inverse of the 12-5 campaign that Daniels and McLaurin helped muster in 2024, which ended with the team in the NFC Championship Game.

But on Monday, August 3, McLaurin told Jeremy Fowler of ESPN that he is at full strength again just six weeks out from the new season and is keyed up for what is to come.

"My body feels great," Mclaurin said. "I'm clocking 22 mph, not missing any days. So I just feel like my normal self. And when you're out here from Day 1 all the way through camp, obviously you get in that full conditioning mode. … This has been my home for going on eight years now, and I'm super excited just to be here for the whole entire season."

GettyWashington Commanders rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams.

McLaurin back at full strength, alongside Daniels also at 100 percent, is a huge boon for the Commanders offense. That said, there are still multiple WR slots waiting for someone to step up and fill them.

ESPN's John Keim wrote Monday that the wideout position battle is the most compelling on Washington's roster this summer on multiple levels.

"Washington probably will mix and match depending on the matchups and the game plan, but players still have to earn time — whether it's third-round pick Antonio Williams or past draft choices Jaylin Lane and Luke McCaffrey," Keim wrote. "The Commanders also have veterans Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and Van Jefferson. So the battle is not only to earn time as a No. 2 but also potentially just for a roster spot."

GettyFree agent wide receiver Stefon Diggs.

One card the Commanders may still have to play is attempting to sign Stefon Diggs in free agency.

Diggs, who was the leading receiver on a New England Patriots team that played in the Super Bowl in February, has as much interest in Washington as the Commanders have in him.

"I'm told free agent Stefon Diggs is on the radar," Fowler reported Tuesday. "Washington is monitoring the situation with Diggs, who's intrigued by the chance to play in Washington (he's from the area). Let's see how things play out, but it seems like this is a realistic option as the sides keep in contact."
